### ACCESS RULES

> These rules are enforced by Supabase RLS policies — they run inside the database engine, not in browser code, so they cannot be bypassed from the frontend.

| Entity | Read | Create | Update | Delete |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `users` | Own row only **(customer)**; all rows **(groomer)** | Created automatically by Supabase Auth on signup | Own row **(customer)**, but `role` column is excluded from customer update policies; any row **(groomer)** | Nobody in V1 |
| `dogs` | Own dogs only **(customer)**; all dogs **(groomer)** | Customer (own dogs only) | Own dogs **(customer)**; any dog **(groomer)** | Customer (own dogs only) |
| `bookings` | Own bookings only **(customer)**; all bookings **(groomer)** | Customer (sets `customer_id` = own id) | Groomer only (status changes, confirmations); deposit_paid set only by Edge Function | Nobody in V1 |

**The "must NEVER" rule is enforced here:** A customer's RLS policy on `users` is `id = auth.uid()`. Even if a customer's browser made a raw database query, the database would return only their own row. Addresses and phone numbers of other customers are never returned.

## 4. Trust Boundaries

### What runs in the browser (untrusted)

- React UI components and all form inputs
- Displaying data that has already been fetched and filtered by RLS
- Calling Supabase with the user's session token (a JWT — a cryptographically signed string that proves who you are; Supabase issues one at login)
- Stripe.js (Stripe's own browser library) — collects card details and exchanges them for a **payment method ID** (a temporary token representing the card, safe to send to your server; the actual card number never touches your code)

### What runs on the server (trusted)

- **All Stripe secret-key operations:** creating a payment intent, confirming a charge, processing webhook events
- **All Twilio calls:** building and sending SMS messages
- **RLS policies:** run inside PostgreSQL on Supabase's servers
- **Role enforcement:** `role` lives in the database; customers cannot update it because the RLS update policy explicitly excludes that column

### ⚠️ Lovable's known problem

Lovable generates Vite-based React. Vite environment variables prefixed with `VITE_` are **baked into the JavaScript bundle that ships to the browser** — anyone can open DevTools and read them. Lovable may suggest putting `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` or `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` in a `VITE_` variable. **Never do this.** The only keys safe in `VITE_` variables are:

- `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` — public, fine
- `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — public, fine (RLS limits what it can access)
- `VITE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` — public by design (it's Stripe's own term for the browser-safe key)

Every other key belongs in Supabase Edge Function environment variables, which stay on the server.

### Login token in the PWA

Supabase Auth's JavaScript library stores the JWT in **`localStorage`** by default (browser memory that persists across sessions). Any JavaScript running on the same page can read it. For V1, with no third-party scripts on the page, this is an acceptable risk. **Rule: never add analytics scripts, chat widgets, or any third-party `<script>` tags without reviewing this trade-off first.** If you later need hardened token storage, Supabase's server-side rendering client can use httpOnly cookies (cookies the browser stores but JavaScript cannot read), but that requires a more complex setup outside Lovable's current scope.

### File storage

Dog photos are stored in a **private Supabase Storage bucket** — no file has a permanent public URL. The app requests a **signed URL** (a temporary link that expires, typically in one hour) each time a photo needs to be displayed. A signed URL for customer A's dog photo will not work if customer B somehow obtains it after it expires.

| Service | Purpose | Key(s) | Where stored | Free-tier limits | If it goes down |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions | `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (browser-safe); `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (bypasses RLS — server only) | Anon key in Lovable `VITE_` env vars; service role key in Edge Function secrets | Free: 500 MB DB, 1 GB storage, 50,000 monthly active users, 500,000 Edge Function calls/month | App goes offline; Supabase targets 99.9% uptime on paid tier; free tier has no SLA |
| **Stripe** | $20 deposit per booking | `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` (browser); `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` (server); `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (server) | Publishable key in `VITE_` env; secret + webhook secret in Edge Function secrets | No monthly fee; **2.9% + $0.30 per transaction** | New bookings can't collect deposit; existing bookings unaffected; add a "pay at appointment" fallback in V2 |
| **Twilio** | SMS reminder the day before each appointment | `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` + `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | Edge Function secrets only | Pay-as-you-go; approximately $0.008 per US SMS; no monthly minimum | Reminders don't send; bookings still work; consider adding email reminders as a backup |

### Reminder scheduling

A Supabase Edge Function with a **cron trigger** (a task scheduled to run automatically on a repeating schedule, like "every day at 9 AM") queries all bookings for the following day and fires a Twilio SMS to each customer. The cron function uses the `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` to read across all customer rows (this is safe because the function runs entirely on the server).

### ⚠️ US business texting registration (10DLC)

**10DLC** stands for 10-Digit Long Code — the standard US phone number format businesses use to send texts. The US government requires companies to register their texting campaign with an organization called The Campaign Registry before sending bulk messages. Twilio enforces this. **Registration takes 2–6 weeks and involves a small fee (check Twilio's current pricing, as it changes).** Start this process before you start building, or plan to launch without SMS reminders.

### In-app purchases note

Not applicable. GroomGo is a PWA (not an App Store app) charging for a physical in-person service. Apple and Google's in-app purchase requirements do not apply.

## 7. Decisions Log

These are final unless you explicitly change them.

1. **ADR-1:** Build as PWA, not an App Store app, because Lovable only produces web apps and the builder has no terminal access.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase for database, auth, storage, and serverless functions because it bundles all backend services and Lovable integrates with it directly.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Stripe for deposit payments because the builder already has an account and Stripe's documentation is the clearest available.
4. **ADR-4:** Use Twilio for SMS reminders because it is the most reliable SMS API and supports cron-triggered Edge Functions.
5. **ADR-5:** Store `role` in the `users` table on the server because the browser cannot be trusted to hold permission data.
6. **ADR-6:** Store all secret keys (Stripe secret key, Twilio auth token, Supabase service role key) in Supabase Edge Function environment variables only — never in `VITE_` frontend variables.
7. **ADR-7:** Enforce customer data isolation with Supabase RLS policies so customers can never read another customer's address or phone number, even with a direct API call.
8. **ADR-8:** Serve all dog photos through time-limited signed URLs from a private Supabase Storage bucket; no photo has a permanent public link.

## 8. Known Risks

**Risk 1 — Lovable writes a secret key to the frontend**
Lovable may generate code that puts `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` in a `VITE_` variable or calls Stripe's charge API directly from React. *Mitigation:* Before every deploy, search the generated code for `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, and `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. Any file that contains one of those strings must be an Edge Function, not a React component. Treat this as a launch blocker.

**Risk 2 — An RLS misconfiguration exposes a customer's address**
A single wrong policy could let customer A query customer B's row. *Mitigation:* Before launch, create two test customer accounts and confirm that logging in as customer A and requesting customer B's user row returns zero results. Do this manually in Supabase's table editor and via the app. Treat a failure here as a launch blocker.

**Risk 3 — 10DLC registration delay blocks SMS reminders at launch**
Twilio registration can take 2–6 weeks. *Mitigation:* Start the Twilio registration process this week, before writing any code. If it isn't approved by launch, fall back to reminder emails via Supabase's built-in email sending (limited but free) until SMS is active.

**Risk 4 — Deposit marked paid before Stripe confirms the charge**
If the app marks `deposit_paid = true` based on a message from the browser ("the customer paid!"), a bad actor could lie. *Mitigation:* `deposit_paid` is only ever set to `true` inside the Stripe webhook Edge Function, after Supabase receives a `payment_intent.succeeded` event directly from Stripe's servers. The browser is never trusted to confirm a payment.

**Risk 5 — Supabase free tier limits reached**
500 MB of database fills faster than expected if photos land in the database. 50,000 monthly active users is generous for V1, but if GroomGo grows quickly it could be hit. *Mitigation:* Dog photos always go into Supabase Storage buckets, never as base64 in a database column. Check Supabase's usage dashboard monthly. Budget for the $25/month Pro tier upgrade if needed (it fits within $50 budget alongside Lovable).

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website, not an App Store app.** Customers open it in Safari or Chrome on their phone and can save it to their home screen so it looks and feels like a real app. They won't find it by searching the App Store — that's the main thing they give up, and it directly conflicts with what they asked for. A future workaround exists but requires extra help beyond this stage.

- **All your data lives in one place (Supabase), and the database itself enforces privacy.** Think of it as a spreadsheet where the database engine physically blocks one customer from ever seeing another customer's row — Marisol's address and phone number are invisible to everyone except Marisol.

- **Money is handled by a secure go-between.** Your website collects the card details through Stripe's own form, then passes a temporary stand-in token to a small background program. That program does the actual charge using a key that the customer's phone never sees. The website is like a teller window; the key is in the vault behind it.

- **Reminder texts need paperwork that takes weeks.** To legally send business text messages in the US you have to register with a government-linked registry through Twilio. This is not optional and not instant. Start the registration this week, before any coding begins.

- **You're right at your budget ceiling at scale.** Building and testing costs roughly $20/month. At a hundred customers it's about $21/month. At a thousand customers you bump into the $50/month ceiling. The only knob to turn is the Supabase plan — keep photos out of the database and watch the dashboard monthly.

---

## 10. Accounts to Set Up Before Building

No Apple Developer Program or Google Play Console accounts are needed (PWA, not App Store).

- [x] **Stripe** — you already have this. Action needed: enable Stripe webhooks in your Stripe dashboard (Dashboard → Developers → Webhooks → Add endpoint). No cost, no approval wait.
- [ ] **Supabase** — sign up free at supabase.com. Create a new project. No approval needed, live in minutes.
- [ ] **Lovable (Pro tier)** — check current pricing at lovable.dev before signing up; tiers change. You need at least the plan that allows custom domains and publishing. Estimated ~$20/month.
- [ ] **Twilio** — sign up at twilio.com. Buy a 10-digit US phone number (~$1/month). **Immediately start 10DLC registration** (Messaging → Senders → Register). You'll need your business name and a brief description of what texts you'll send. Registration fee and timeline change — check Twilio's current documentation. **Expect 2–6 weeks.**
- [ ] **Custom domain** (optional but recommended) — register something like `groomgo.app` or `groomgo.co` at Namecheap or Cloudflare Registrar (~$10–15/year). Point it at your Lovable-published app.

---

## Context Carry

**Platforms:** PWA only (iPhone and Android via phone browser / Add to Home Screen; not App Store or Google Play).
**Stack:** React (Lovable) → Supabase (PostgreSQL + RLS + Auth + Storage + Edge Functions) + Stripe (deposits) + Twilio (SMS reminders via daily cron Edge Function).
**Entities:** `users` (id, name, phone, address, role), `dogs` (id, owner_id, name, breed, notes, photo_url), `bookings` (id, customer_id, dog_id, slot_datetime, status, deposit_paid, stripe_payment_intent_id).
**Trust rules:** All secret keys in Edge Function env vars only; role stored in DB, customers blocked from updating it by RLS; RLS `id = auth.uid()` isolates every customer to their own row; dog photos in private Storage bucket served via expiring signed URLs; `deposit_paid` set only by Stripe webhook Edge Function.
**ADRs:** PWA not App Store (1); Supabase for all backend (2); Stripe for payments (3); Twilio for SMS (4); role server-side in DB (5); secrets in Edge Functions only (6); RLS for data isolation (7); signed URLs for photos (8).

## 3. Data Model

> **Glossary:** A **UUID** is a globally unique ID (looks like `a8f3d2…`). A **timestamptz** is a date + time including timezone. An **FK** (foreign key) is a column that points to a specific row in another table, creating a relationship. An **index** is a shortcut the database builds so it can find rows quickly without scanning the whole table.

| `id` | `uuid` PK | Same value as `auth.users.id` — links auth identity to this profile |
| `role` | `text` | `'customer'` or `'groomer'`; default `'customer'`; **only writable via service_role** |
| `full_name` | `text` | Display name |

### ACCESS RULES (enforced in Supabase RLS — not just in the UI)

| Entity | Customer — own rows | Customer — another customer's rows | Groomer (Marisol) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profiles` (name, phone, address) | Read ✅  Update ✅ | ❌ **BLOCKED AT DATABASE LEVEL** | Read all ✅ |
| `profiles.role` | Read own ✅  Update ❌ | ❌ **BLOCKED** | Read all ✅; set via service_role only |
| `dogs` | Create ✅ Read ✅ Update ✅ Delete ✅ (own only) | ❌ **BLOCKED** | Read all ✅ |
| `dog photos` (Storage) | Upload ✅  Read via signed URL ✅ (own dogs only) | ❌ **BLOCKED** | Read all via signed URL ✅ |
| `bookings` | Create ✅  Read ✅ (own)  Cancel own ✅ | ❌ **BLOCKED** | Read all ✅  Update all ✅ |

> The spec rule — **customers must NEVER see other customers' addresses or phone numbers** — is enforced by RLS at the database layer. Even if someone bypassed the UI entirely and called the Supabase API directly with their own login token, the database would refuse to return another customer's row. This is not a UI trick; it is a database rule.

## 4. Trust Boundaries

> **Plain English:** "Untrusted" = code that runs on the user's device. Anyone can open browser developer tools and read every variable in it. "Trusted" = code that runs on a server the user can never touch.

---

### Untrusted (runs in the user's browser / phone)
- The entire React UI — all buttons, forms, and pages
- **Stripe.js** — Stripe's own JavaScript library; it collects card details and sends them *directly to Stripe's servers*, so card numbers never pass through Supabase or Lovable
- The **Supabase anon key** — this key is intentionally public (it's Supabase's design). It's like a restaurant's public phone number. It only unlocks what RLS explicitly permits; by itself it cannot see any customer data

### Trusted (runs on Supabase's servers — no user can access this)
- All Edge Functions and every environment variable inside them
- `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` — used to create Payment Intents server-side
- `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — used to verify that a webhook truly came from Stripe
- `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` and `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` — used to send SMS
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — used inside Edge Functions for trusted database writes; bypasses RLS intentionally only for system operations (marking `deposit_paid = true`)
- All RLS policy logic — these live in PostgreSQL, not in JavaScript

---

### ⚠️ Lovable-specific warning — check this before going live

Lovable's AI code generator sometimes places secret keys in the wrong location. Specifically:

1. **Watch for `VITE_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` in any React file.** Vite (the underlying build tool Lovable uses) automatically bundles any environment variable whose name starts with `VITE_` into the browser-downloadable JavaScript. Anyone can open their browser's developer tools and read it. `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` must only ever appear in Edge Function code — never in `/src`.
2. **Watch for `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` in any React component.** Same issue.
3. **Watch for any secret in a `VITE_` variable at all.** Only the Supabase anon key and Stripe's publishable key (the one that starts with `pk_`) are safe in the frontend.
4. **Check that RLS is ON for every table.** In the Supabase Dashboard: Table Editor → select each table → confirm the "Row Level Security" toggle is enabled. Supabase creates new tables with RLS *off* by default.

---

### Role storage — how the groomer role is protected

- Each user's role (`'customer'` or `'groomer'`) lives in the `profiles.role` column in the PostgreSQL database.
- The RLS `UPDATE` policy on `profiles` explicitly prevents any user from changing their own `role` value — it checks that the role in the updated row matches what is already stored.
- Marisol's role is set **once, manually**, using the Supabase Dashboard's Table Editor (a web interface — no terminal required). Nobody else ever touches it.
- The role is **not** stored in localStorage, browser cookies, or any editable user metadata field. Only the database decides who is the groomer. A customer cannot promote themselves by editing their profile.

---

### File storage — dog photos

- All photos are stored in a **private** Supabase Storage bucket named `dog-photos`. There is no public URL for any file.
- To display a photo, the React UI calls an Edge Function, which checks the requester's identity, confirms they own that dog (or are Marisol), and returns an **expiring signed URL** — a one-time-use link that becomes dead after one hour.
- No customer can ever retrieve a URL for another customer's dog photo, even if they know the file path.

---

### Login token — how it is stored (PWA / web)

- After login, Supabase Auth issues a **JWT** (a digital session pass, valid for 1 hour) and a **refresh token** (used to silently get a new JWT without logging in again).
- Supabase's JavaScript client stores these in **localStorage** by default. This is the standard Supabase approach for web apps and is acceptable for a booking app. The JWT's short 1-hour lifetime limits the window of risk if it were ever exposed.
- Stripe card data is handled entirely by Stripe.js and is **never written to localStorage, Supabase, or any server Marisol controls**.

---

### Deep links (links in SMS messages)

- The day-before reminder SMS will contain a link like `https://groomgo.app/bookings/[booking-id]`.
- Every page that displays personal data (booking details, addresses, dog info) checks the user's session JWT when it loads. An unauthenticated visitor is redirected to the login page immediately — the content never renders.
- The booking ID in the URL is a UUID. Even if someone guessed another booking's UUID, the RLS policy would refuse to serve that booking's data to anyone who isn't the booking's owner or Marisol.
- No link in the app bypasses a login check or a permission check.

---

> **A2P 10DLC** — Application-to-Person, 10-Digit Long Code. US mobile carriers now require businesses to register before sending bulk SMS or their messages are silently filtered. Registration takes 2–6 weeks. **Start this on day one.**

Publishable key: Lovable frontend | No monthly fee; 2.9% + $0.30 per successful charge | Block new bookings; show "Payment temporarily unavailable, please call Marisol" |

Service role: Edge Function env **only** | Free: 500 MB DB, 1 GB storage, 50,000 MAU, 500K Edge Function calls/month. **⚠️ Free projects are automatically paused after 1 week of inactivity** — use Pro for production | App is fully offline; no workaround. ### App Store / In-App Purchase rules

The $20 deposit is payment for an **in-person, real-world service** (a dog grooming visit at the customer's home). **Apple and Google do not require you to use their in-app purchase system for physical or in-person services.** You are permitted to charge via Stripe on a web page. Stripe keeps 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction; Apple and Google take **nothing** from these payments.

## 7. Decisions Log

These are final unless you explicitly change them.

1. **ADR-1:** Use Lovable / React for the frontend because it is the chosen build tool and requires no terminal.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase as the sole backend because it provides database, auth, file storage, and serverless functions in one managed service with first-class Lovable integration.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Supabase Row Level Security for all data access control because it operates at the database layer and cannot be bypassed by frontend code.
4. **ADR-4:** Run all calls to Stripe and Twilio inside Supabase Edge Functions so that every secret key stays off the browser.
5. **ADR-5:** Use Stripe for the $20 deposit because the user already has a verified account and it is the industry standard for web payments.
6. **ADR-6:** Use Twilio for SMS reminders because it is the best-documented SMS provider for Supabase Edge Function integration.
7. **ADR-7:** Build as a Progressive Web App (PWA) rather than an App Store app because Lovable cannot produce native apps and the user has no terminal access.
8. **ADR-8:** Store the `role` field in `profiles.role` in the database, updateable only via the Supabase service role, so no user can self-promote to groomer.
9. **ADR-9:** Store all dog photos in a private Supabase Storage bucket and serve them exclusively through expiring signed URLs.
10. **ADR-10:** Use Supabase pg_cron for the daily SMS reminder job to avoid adding any additional scheduling service.

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website, not a native app.** Customers open a URL in their phone's browser. They can save it to their home screen so it looks like an app. It works well — it just cannot be found in the App Store, which is a trade-off you are making in exchange for building it quickly and cheaply.

- **One company (Supabase) handles almost everything behind the scenes.** Your customer data, logins, dog photos, and the secure code that charges cards all live inside Supabase. If Supabase has an outage, the app is down — but Supabase is extremely reliable and used by thousands of businesses globally.

- **The database itself enforces privacy, not just the app.** The rule "customers must never see each other's addresses" is written into the database as a locked rule. Even if someone found a bug in the website code, the database would still refuse to show them another customer's information. It is not a UI trick.

- **Your card-charging key and your texting key never leave the server.** When a customer pays, their browser just says "please charge this card" to a secure server function. The actual charging happens on the server, where your Stripe key lives. Nobody browsing the website can ever find or steal it.

- **You need to register your texting number with US phone carriers before launch, and it takes weeks.** Without this registration (called A2P 10DLC), the reminder texts Marisol's customers expect the day before their appointment will be silently blocked. ## 1. Stack Decision

> **Terms used here for the first time:**
> - **Row-level security (RLS):** database rules that run *inside* the database, enforcing who can see which rows — not just rules in the app code, which can be bypassed.
> - **Serverless function (Edge Function):** a small piece of server-side code that runs on demand, without you managing any server.
> - **Managed service:** a third-party company runs and maintains the infrastructure; you configure it in a dashboard.
> - **JWT (JSON Web Token):** a short-lived digital pass your browser holds after login to prove your identity on every request.

### Useful Indexes

| Index | Why it helps |

| `bookings(customer_id)` | Fast lookup of a customer's own bookings |
| `bookings(slot_id)` | Check if a slot is already booked |

---

### Access Rules

| Entity | Customer reads | Customer creates | Customer updates | Customer deletes | Groomer reads | Groomer creates | Groomer updates | Groomer deletes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `profiles` | **Own row only** ⚠️ | Own row at sign-up | Own row, **never `role`** | No | **All rows** | No | Any row | No |
| `dogs` | Own dogs only | Own dogs | Own dogs | Own dogs | All | Yes (walk-ins) | Any | Any |
| `slots` | All (read calendar) | No | No | No | All | Yes | Any field | Yes |
| `bookings` | Own bookings only | Own (customer_id must = own user ID) | Cancel only (set `status = 'cancelled'`) | No | All | Yes | Any field | Yes |

⚠️ The **"customers must NEVER see other customers' addresses or phone numbers"** rule is enforced inside the database via RLS: a customer's query on `profiles` returns only the single row where `id = their own user ID`. The app code cannot override this — the database rejects the query if it violates the rule.

---

## 4. Trust Boundaries

### Untrusted side — the browser

Everything running in the browser is visible to the person using it. This includes:
- All of the React app code Lovable generates
- Form values before they are sent
- The JWT (login token) stored in browser memory

**Nothing secret lives here.**

### Trusted side — the server

- Supabase Edge Functions — where Stripe and Twilio keys live
- The PostgreSQL database with RLS policies
- Stripe's own servers (the hosted Checkout page)
- Twilio's API servers

### Rules that must hold

1. **Stripe secret key** (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`) and **Stripe webhook signing secret** (`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) live only in Supabase Edge Function environment variables — never in the React app.
2. **Payment confirmation is server-side only.** The Edge Function receives Stripe's webhook, checks the **cryptographic signature** (a mathematical proof that the message truly came from Stripe, not a fake), then sets `deposit_paid = true`. The browser cannot do this step. A customer cannot mark their own booking as paid.
3. **Twilio credentials** (`TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`) live only in Edge Function environment variables.
4. **Row-level security is the last line of defence.** Even if Lovable generates a poorly-written query, the database itself rejects it if it would violate RLS.

### Where the role is stored, and why users cannot fake it

`role` lives in the `profiles` table in the database. A **database trigger** (an automatic rule the database runs before any update happens) raises an error if someone tries to change their own `role` column. Only a database administrator — you, using the Supabase dashboard — can promote someone to groomer.

> **⚠️ Lovable risk to watch for:** Lovable sometimes stores user profile data in Supabase `user_metadata`, which *is* editable by the logged-in user. Role must live in the `profiles` table with the trigger — not in `user_metadata`. Verify this after Lovable generates the sign-up flow.

**Setting Marisol as groomer:** After she creates her account, you open the Supabase dashboard, find her row in `profiles`, and set `role = 'groomer'`. She cannot do this herself, and no one else can either.

### Login token in the browser

Supabase Auth in a React SPA (a website that behaves like an app — what Lovable builds) stores the login token in `localStorage` — a place in the browser where websites save small amounts of data.

- This is **not** an httpOnly cookie (a stricter kind of browser storage that JavaScript itself cannot read, making token theft much harder).
- The main attack that exploits `localStorage` tokens is called **XSS** (cross-site scripting — injecting malicious code into the page). React automatically escapes all displayed content, which blocks this attack in the vast majority of cases.
- Supabase access tokens expire after **1 hour** and refresh automatically — so even if a token were stolen, the attacker's window is short.
- This is the accepted tradeoff for React single-page apps and is appropriate for a dog-grooming booking service.

### Dog photos

- Stored in a **private** Supabase Storage bucket — not publicly accessible by URL.
- Displayed via **signed URLs**: time-limited links (for example, valid for 1 hour) that the app generates fresh each time a photo needs to be shown. The URL expires and cannot be bookmarked or shared permanently.

> **⚠️ Lovable risk to watch for:** Lovable may default to creating a **public** storage bucket. After the initial build, verify in the Supabase dashboard that the dog-photo bucket is set to **private**, and that photo display in the app uses signed URLs rather than direct public URLs.

### Deep links

Any URL that shows booking details or a customer's address must require a valid login session. RLS is the safety net inside the database, but the frontend should redirect unauthenticated visitors to the login screen rather than showing an access error.

---

## 5. External Services

| Service | Purpose | Key(s) | Where stored | Free tier / cost | If it goes down |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | Database, auth, storage, edge functions, cron | `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (admin); `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (public — safe by design, RLS protects data) | Service key in Edge Function env vars; anon key in the React app (intentional) | Free: 500 MB DB, 1 GB storage, 2 GB bandwidth, 500K edge function calls/month. Pro: ~$25/month | App cannot load or save anything; wait for Supabase to recover; all data stays intact |
| **Stripe** | $20 deposit payment | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Edge Function env vars **only** | No monthly fee; ~2.9% + $0.30 per transaction ≈ $0.88 deducted from each $20 deposit | Customers see a payment error; no booking data is lost; they can retry when Stripe recovers |
| **Twilio** | SMS reminders day before appointment | `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | Edge Function env vars **only** | ~$0.008/message; **~$10–25/month for required 10DLC campaign + ~$15–25 one-time registration fee** | Reminder not sent; booking still exists; `reminder_sent` stays `false` so you can resend manually |
| **Lovable** | Frontend hosting | None (managed internally) | — | Verify current pricing at lovable.dev; a paid plan is likely required for a production app | App is inaccessible; all data in Supabase is safe; wait for Lovable to recover |

**Stripe and in-app purchase rules:**
Dog grooming is an in-person service, not a digital product. Apple and Google do **not** require their in-app purchase system for in-person services — Stripe is permitted and neither platform takes a cut. (This applies even if you ever move to a native app — verify against current store guidelines at that time, as rules change.)

---

### ⚠️ 10DLC — This Affects Your Launch Date

**10DLC** (10-digit long code) is the US carrier system that requires any business sending SMS from an application to register their number and campaign before messages go through. Without registration, carriers silently filter or block the messages.

- Approval takes **2 to 8 weeks**
- Campaign registration costs roughly **$10–25/month** plus a **~$15–25 one-time fee**
- You cannot reliably send reminder texts until approved
- **Start this process on Day 1 of building — not the week before launch**

Twilio walks you through the full registration in their dashboard.

---

## 6. Cost at 0 / 100 / 1,000 Users

*Stripe fees are deducted from each payment before it reaches Marisol — she receives approximately $19.12 per $20 deposit. This is not a separate monthly bill.*

| Scenario | Lovable | Supabase | Twilio 10DLC fee | Twilio SMS | Monthly total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 users — app live, no bookings | ~$25 † | $0 (free tier) | ~$10 | $0 | **~$35** |
| 100 users, ~80 bookings/month | ~$25 † | $0 (free tier) | ~$10 | <$1 | **~$36** |
| 1,000 users, ~800 bookings/month | ~$25 † | ~$25 (Pro) | ~$10 | ~$6 | **~$66** |

† Verify current Lovable plan pricing at lovable.dev — pricing changes.

**Budget note:** You are within your $50/month target at 0–100 users. At 1,000 users the Supabase Pro upgrade adds ~$25/month, putting you ~$16 over budget. The main levers are Lovable's plan tier and staying within Supabase's free-tier limits. You can delay the Pro upgrade as long as Supabase's free tier isn't exhausted.

---

## 7. Decisions Log

These are final unless you explicitly change them.

- **ADR-1:** Use Lovable for the frontend because it is the stated build tool and requires no code.
- **ADR-2:** Use Supabase for database, auth, storage, and edge functions because it pairs natively with Lovable, has built-in row-level security, and offers a generous free tier.
- **ADR-3:** Build a web app, not a native app, because Lovable cannot produce App Store apps and the budget and no-terminal constraints rule out a separate native build tool.
- **ADR-4:** Use Stripe Checkout (Stripe's hosted payment page) for the $20 deposit because the user already has Stripe, card data never touches the app, and a webhook confirms payment server-side.
- **ADR-5:** Verify the Stripe payment webhook inside a Supabase Edge Function — never the frontend — because secret keys must never run in the browser.
- **ADR-6:** Use Twilio for SMS reminders because it is well-documented, supports 10DLC registration, and integrates cleanly from an Edge Function.
- **ADR-7:** Use Supabase row-level security to enforce data isolation because customers must never see other customers' addresses or phone numbers.
- **ADR-8:** Store the user role in the `profiles` database table protected by a trigger that blocks self-update — not in editable Supabase auth metadata.
- **ADR-9:** Store dog photos in a private Supabase Storage bucket and serve them only via expiring signed URLs.
- **ADR-10:** Run the nightly reminder via a Supabase Cron Job that triggers an Edge Function, keeping all Twilio credentials server-side.

---

## 8. Known Risks

**1. 10DLC registration delay**
The carrier approval process for business SMS takes 2–8 weeks. If you don't start on Day 1, reminder texts won't work at launch.
*Mitigation: start Twilio 10DLC registration the same day you create the Twilio account. As a fallback, send email reminders for the first weeks of operation.*

**2. Lovable puts a secret key in the browser**
Lovable's AI code generator may produce a Stripe or Twilio call that runs in the React app instead of an Edge Function, exposing the secret key to anyone who opens browser developer tools.
*Mitigation: after each major Lovable build session, search the generated JavaScript for the strings `STRIPE_SECRET` and `TWILIO`. Neither should appear. If they do, the call must be moved to an Edge Function.*

**3. Dog-photo bucket accidentally set to public**
If Supabase Storage defaults to a public bucket, photo URLs are permanent and guessable by anyone.
*Mitigation: after Lovable generates the initial app, immediately verify in the Supabase dashboard that the bucket is marked private. Confirm that the app requests a fresh signed URL each time it displays a photo, rather than storing or displaying a direct URL.*

**4. Double-booking the same slot**
Two customers choosing the same slot at the same moment could both create bookings before either one is rejected.
*Mitigation: add a database uniqueness constraint on `bookings(slot_id)` for all non-cancelled bookings. This constraint lives in the database, not the app code, so it cannot be bypassed. Alternatively, have an Edge Function reserve a slot atomically — a **database transaction** is a group of changes that either all succeed or all fail together — before redirecting to Stripe.*

**5. Supabase free-tier project pauses**
Supabase has historically paused free projects after a period of inactivity (check the current policy in their docs — it has been approximately one week). During early development when the app sits idle, the database could pause.
*Mitigation: log into the Supabase dashboard regularly during development to keep the project active; upgrade to Supabase Pro before inviting real customers, so pausing cannot happen during live use.*

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **The "no peeking at other customers" rule is enforced by the database, not just the screen.** Even if someone technically sophisticated tried to bypass the app's front end, the database itself blocks any query that would return another customer's address or phone number. It's like a vault with its own combination lock, independent of the door.
- **You never see or store credit card numbers.** When a customer pays the $20 deposit, they enter their card on a page that Stripe controls and hosts — not your app. Your app only ever hears "paid" or "not paid."
- **Reminder texts go out automatically every night.** A scheduled program wakes up, checks which appointments are the next day, and sends a text to each of those customers. Marisol doesn't need to do anything manually.
- **The app lives on the web, not the App Store.** Customers open it in their phone's browser and can add a shortcut to their home screen. It will not appear when they search the App Store. You should tell customers how to get to it — a link on a business card, a QR code, a text from Marisol. This is a real limitation compared to what they asked for, and it is worth communicating upfront.
- **Almost everything depends on one company: Supabase.** Customer data, login, photos, and automated texts all run through Supabase. If Supabase has an outage, the app goes offline. The tradeoff is that one service handles everything cheaply, with no servers for you to maintain.

---

## 10. Accounts to Set Up Before Building

| Account | Purpose | Cost | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lovable** — lovable.dev | Build and host the web app | Verify current plan pricing at lovable.dev | A paid plan is likely required for a production deployment with a custom domain |
| **Supabase** — supabase.com | Database, login, file storage, server functions, cron | Free to start; Pro ~$25/month | Free projects may pause after inactivity — check the current policy; plan to upgrade to Pro before launch |
| **Stripe** ✓ *you already have this* | Accept $20 deposits | No monthly fee; ~2.9% + $0.30 per transaction | Make sure the account is in **Live mode** (not Test mode) before launch |
| **Twilio** — twilio.com | SMS appointment reminders | ~$0.008/message + ~$10–25/month for 10DLC campaign + ~$15–25 one-time registration fee | **⚠️ Start 10DLC registration immediately — approval takes 2–8 weeks** |

**10DLC checklist inside Twilio (do this first):**

- [ ] Create Twilio account
- [ ] Purchase one US 10-digit long-code phone number (~$1/month)
- [ ] Register your **brand** (your name or business name, and either an EIN or SSN if you're a sole proprietor)
- [ ] Register your **campaign** (select "Appointment Reminders" as the use case)
- [ ] Submit and wait — do not expect SMS delivery to work until approval is confirmed
- [ ] Send test messages to your own phone to confirm delivery before launching

No Apple Developer Program or Google Play Console account is needed — we are building a web app, not a native app.

---

## Context Carry

**Platforms:** Web app only (browser + home-screen shortcut on iPhone and Android). Not listed in the App Store or Google Play.

**Stack:** Lovable (React, hosted) · Supabase (PostgreSQL + RLS, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Cron) · Stripe Checkout + server-side webhook · Twilio SMS.

# ARCHITECTURE.md — FormCoach

---

## App-Store App vs Home-Screen Web App

Before the architecture, this question must be answered first.

**My recommendation: a home-screen web app (called a PWA — Progressive Web App).**

A PWA is a website that behaves like an app. Users open it in Safari (iPhone) or Chrome (Android) and tap "Add to Home Screen" — no App Store required.

**Why PWA specifically for FormCoach:** Your spec says you want to take $9.99/month through Stripe directly. Apple's App Store rules require that subscriptions for digital features sold inside a native iOS app must go through Apple's own payment system — Apple keeps 15–30% of every payment. Google Play has the same rule. A PWA lives outside any app store, so those rules don't apply. You keep roughly 97% of each payment (Stripe takes about 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction).

**What your users give up with a PWA:**
- The app cannot be found in the App Store or Google Play. Members find it through a link you share or your website.
- On iPhone, installing requires extra steps: open Safari → tap the Share button → tap "Add to Home Screen." Some users will need guidance.
- Push notifications on iPhone are limited: they only work on iOS 16.4 or later, and only after the user has installed the PWA to their home screen.
- The feel is slightly less polished than a native app — no vibration feedback, slightly different scrolling on some screens.

**What you gain:**
- Full Stripe revenue (~97% per payment vs. ~70–85% with Apple/Google).
- No Apple Developer Program fee (currently $99/year — verify at developer.apple.com).
- No Google Play Console fee (currently $25 one-time — verify at play.google.com/console).
- Updates go live the moment you deploy — zero app store review delays.
- One codebase for all platforms.

Since I am recommending a PWA, the MOBILE-specific notes in sections 1, 5, and 10 are skipped per the blueprint rules.

---

## 1. Stack Decision

**Plain English:** This table is every technology layer the app will use, why it was chosen, and what was rejected.

"Serverless" means code that runs on demand on someone else's computer — you don't manage any server yourself; it starts when a request arrives and stops when it's done.

| Layer | Choice | Why | Rejected alternative & reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | Expo (React Native Web compiled to a PWA) | Your chosen build tool; one codebase runs as a PWA on all devices | Separate native iOS + Android apps — triggers Apple IAP requirement, blocking Stripe direct billing |
| **Backend / API** | Supabase Edge Functions (serverless functions hosted by Supabase) | You already have Supabase; no server to maintain; tight integration with Supabase database, auth, and storage; secret keys stay server-side | Express.js on Fly.io — a separate server to provision and maintain; Vercel Functions — also fine but splits logic across two platforms |
| **Database** | Supabase PostgreSQL | Bundled with your existing account; supports Row Level Security — RLS — an automatic filter the database applies to every query so users only see their own data | PlanetScale / Neon — no existing account, extra complexity |
| **Auth** | Supabase Auth | Bundled with Supabase; handles sign-up, login, password reset, and session tokens; stores the user's role where users cannot modify it (see section 4) | Firebase Auth — no existing account; Clerk — adds monthly cost |
| **File storage** | Supabase Storage (private bucket) | Bundled; private buckets serve files only through signed URLs — time-limited links the server generates on demand; RLS controls who can generate a link | AWS S3 — extra account, more setup; Cloudinary — paid |
| **Payments** | Stripe Checkout + Stripe Customer Portal | You already have an account; Stripe hosts the payment page so you never touch card numbers; webhooks — event notifications Stripe sends your server — keep subscription status up to date automatically | Stripe Elements (embed card form in your app) — more code, more security compliance burden |
| **AI / LLM** | Google Gemini 1.5 Flash (via Google AI API) | Processes short video files natively — no need to break the video into individual frames first; generous free tier; very low per-request cost | OpenAI GPT-4o Vision — more expensive, requires extracting frames from video before sending |
| **Hosting** | Vercel (free Hobby tier) | Deploys Expo web output in one command; free global CDN — a content delivery network, meaning copies of your app files are stored in servers near your users so the app loads fast | Netlify — also fine; Supabase Hosting — still experimental |
| **Email** | Supabase Auth emails + Resend | Supabase sends all authentication emails (welcome, password reset) automatically; Resend's free tier — 3,000 emails/month — handles any transactional messages | SendGrid — more setup; Postmark — no free tier |

**Note on video recording in Expo Web:** Expo's built-in camera component does not work in the browser. ## 4. Trust Boundaries

**Plain English:** "Untrusted" means the code runs on the user's phone, where anyone can open the browser's developer tools and read what's there. "Trusted" means the code runs on your server, where only you can see it. Secret keys and permission checks must always be on the trusted side.

---

### Untrusted — user's phone browser (anyone can inspect this):

- All your Expo/React app code (JavaScript in the browser is readable by anyone)
- **Supabase anon key** — designed to be public; RLS policies in the database enforce what it can actually see
- **Stripe publishable key** — designed to be public; it can only initiate a checkout session, never charge a card directly
- The user's JWT session token (see below)

---

### Trusted — Supabase Edge Functions (only you can see these):

- `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` — creates and modifies subscriptions; must never leave the server
- `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — used to verify that a webhook call genuinely came from Stripe, not an impostor
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` — calls the AI service; must never appear in app code
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — a master key that bypasses RLS for admin operations (e.g. writing subscription status); must never be in the browser

All four are stored as environment variables (private configuration values) in your Edge Function settings, not in code.

---

### Login token in the PWA browser:

Supabase Auth issues a **JWT — a JSON Web Token**, which is a signed digital ID card that proves who the user is. In an Expo Web PWA, this is stored in **`localStorage`** — the browser's built-in storage space, readable by JavaScript on the page.

- The JWT expires after **1 hour**. A stolen JWT is useless after that.
- A **refresh token** (a one-time-use code) is used to get a new JWT silently — the user stays logged in without noticing.
- **HTTPS** (enforced by Vercel) encrypts everything in transit so tokens cannot be intercepted on the network.
- `localStorage` can be read by JavaScript running on the same page. The mitigation is short expiry + HTTPS. This is standard practice for web apps and acceptable for V1.
- If you later want stronger protection, Supabase Auth supports **`httpOnly` cookies** — a type of cookie that JavaScript on the page cannot read at all — but this requires a server-rendered setup (more complexity than Expo Web for now).

---

### Where the user's role is stored, and why they can't change it:

- The role (`member` or `coach`) is stored in Supabase Auth's **`app_metadata`** field — a special section of the auth record that can only be written by the Supabase **service role key** (your server). Users cannot write to `app_metadata` via any API the browser can reach.
- The role is embedded inside every JWT the user receives, and every RLS policy checks it.
- A user cannot promote themselves to coach by editing their profile, calling any public API endpoint, or any other means.
- Assigning the coach role to yourself is a one-time operation done directly in the Supabase dashboard.

---

### Video file access:

- All videos are stored in a **private** Supabase Storage bucket. There is no public URL for any video file.
- To view a video, the server generates a **signed URL** — a time-limited link, valid for 60 minutes, tied to that specific file.
- The RLS policy on Storage checks: `requesting_user.id = form_videos.member_id`. A member can only generate a signed URL for their own video.
- The `storage_path` value in the database (e.g. `videos/user-abc/deadlift-2026-09-27.mp4`) is meaningless without a valid signed URL. Reading the path does not grant access to the file.
- Coach access to videos uses the service role key, server-side only, never exposed to the browser.
- **Members can never access another member's video through any route.**

---

### Deep links (URLs that open the app to a specific page):

Since this is a PWA, "deep links" are ordinary HTTPS URLs (e.g. `https://formcoach.app/workout/today`). Every route in the app checks whether the user is authenticated before rendering any data. If not logged in, the user is redirected to the login screen. No URL skips the authentication or permission check.

## 7. Decisions Log

ADR = Architecture Decision Record. One line each. These are **final** unless you change them and update this file.

1. **ADR-1:** Build as a PWA (not a native app-store app) because selling a digital subscription inside a native iOS app requires Apple IAP, which takes 15–30%, directly conflicting with the Stripe-direct requirement.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase for database, auth, and storage because an existing account is already in place and it covers three critical layers in one service.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Supabase Edge Functions as the API layer because they are built into Supabase, require no separate server to manage, and keep all secret keys server-side.
4. **ADR-4:** Enforce data access with Supabase Row Level Security (RLS) at the database layer because it enforces the "members must never see other members' data" rule regardless of application-level bugs.
5. **ADR-5:** Store user role in Supabase Auth `app_metadata` (not in editable profile fields) because `app_metadata` can only be written by the service role key, so users cannot promote themselves.
6. **ADR-6:** Use Google Gemini 1.5 Flash for AI form analysis because it ingests video natively (no frame extraction required), has a generous free tier, and has a lower per-request cost than OpenAI alternatives.
7. **ADR-7:** Use Stripe Checkout (Stripe's hosted payment page) rather than embedding card fields in the app, to avoid PCI compliance requirements — the security standards governing how card data must be handled — on your own infrastructure.
8. **ADR-8:** Store all form videos in a private Supabase Storage bucket and serve them only via signed (time-limited) URLs, because the spec states members must never see other members' videos.
9. **ADR-9:** Host the PWA on Vercel free tier because the build output is a static site — a collection of files that do not require a running server — and Vercel serves these globally for free at this traffic level.
10. **ADR-10:** Use Resend for transactional email because the free tier covers early-stage volume and setup takes minutes.

## 8. Known Risks

**1. Apple restricts PWA capabilities further on iPhone**
*What:* Apple controls the Safari browser on iPhone. They have historically limited PWA features. If Apple removes "Add to Home Screen," restricts camera access, or limits the `MediaRecorder` API in Safari, the iPhone experience breaks.
*Mitigation:* Monitor Apple WebKit release notes. Design the app so it also works as a plain website in any browser — so even without home-screen installation, members can still use it. Regulatory pressure in the EU may limit Apple's ability to do this.

**2. Video upload fails on poor mobile connections**
*What:* A 10-second phone video is 5–15 MB. On a slow or intermittent connection, the upload may stall or fail.
*Mitigation:* Use Supabase Storage's resumable upload feature (built into their JavaScript client), which can continue a paused upload rather than starting over. Show a clear progress bar. Cap recording at 10 seconds as per spec. Let members retry without re-recording.

**3. Gemini free-tier rate limits cause queued delays at peak times**
*What:* The free tier allows roughly 15 requests per minute. If multiple members upload videos simultaneously, requests queue up and feedback may arrive minutes later rather than instantly.
*Mitigation:* The `ai_status` field already handles async delivery — members see "Analysing…" until feedback arrives. Add a small delay between queued calls. Switch to the Gemini paid tier (very cheap) if average wait exceeds a couple of minutes.

**4. Stripe webhook delivery failure causes subscription status mismatch**
*What:* If the Edge Function that receives Stripe's "payment confirmed" message throws an error, the member's subscription status in the database doesn't update. They could be charged but locked out, or continue access after cancelling.
*Mitigation:* Always return HTTP 200 to Stripe immediately; process the webhook asynchronously afterward. Stripe retries failed webhooks for 72 hours. Add a daily scheduled Edge Function that reconciles subscription status directly against the Stripe API — a safety net that catches any missed webhooks.

**5. Video storage grows unboundedly and exceeds budget**
*What:* At 1,000 members each uploading 5 videos per week, that is ~25 GB of new storage every week. Over months this becomes expensive.
*Mitigation:* Implement a 90-day automatic deletion policy using a scheduled Edge Function. Keep the `ai_feedback` text forever (it's tiny). Clearly inform members in the UI that videos are kept for 90 days.

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website, not an App Store app.** Members open it in their phone's browser and bookmark it to their home screen — no download required. This means you keep nearly all of the $9.99. Stripe takes about 30 cents plus 3%, nothing else.

- **Supabase is doing most of the work behind the scenes.** It stores all your data, handles member login, holds the videos securely, and runs your server-side logic. You're paying for one service and getting four.

- **The privacy rule — members must never see each other's videos or measurements — is enforced inside the database itself, not just in the app.** Even if the app code has a bug, the database will refuse to show one member's data to another. Think of it as a lock that works even when the door handle breaks.

- **Videos go from the member's phone straight to secure cloud storage, then your server sends them to Google's AI for form feedback.** The AI reads the video, writes feedback text back to the database, and the member sees it in the app. Old videos are deleted after 90 days to keep costs low.

- **You never see or store credit card numbers.** When a member subscribes, they're redirected to Stripe's own secure page to enter their card. Stripe tells your app "this person paid" through an automatic notification. Your app checks the notification is genuine, then unlocks their access. You have no payment compliance burden.

## App-Store App vs. Home-Screen Web App — Decide This First

You said it must run on iPhone and Android **and** you want to take $9.99 / month with Stripe so Apple and Google don't take a cut. Those two goals directly conflict with a native app-store app.

**The conflict in plain English:** Apple's App Store rules say that if you sell a digital subscription inside an iOS app — and access to workout plans and form checks is digital — you must use Apple's own payment system, and Apple keeps 15–30 % of every payment. Google Play has the same rule. You cannot use Stripe inside a native app to sell a digital subscription without violating both stores' rules; your app could be removed.

**My recommendation: build a Progressive Web App (PWA).** A PWA is a website that looks and behaves like an app. Users open it in their phone's browser (Safari on iPhone, Chrome on Android) and tap "Add to Home Screen" to get an icon. No app store is involved, no store takes a cut, and you can use Stripe freely. Expo supports web builds, so your build tool works exactly as-is — you run `expo export --platform web` and it compiles your React Native code to run in any mobile browser.

```
├── status          text  DEFAULT 'pending'
│                          ← 'pending'|'processing'|'completed'|'failed'
└── uploaded_at     timestamptz
```

**Useful indexes:**
- `profiles(role)` — filtering by coach vs. member
- `profiles(stripe_customer_id)` — Stripe webhook lookups
- `workouts(member_id, planned_date)` — "show me today's workout"
- `sets(workout_id)` — load all sets for one session
- `form_videos(member_id)` — a member's video history
- `form_videos(workout_id)` — all videos for one session

### Access Rules

RLS policies are the enforcement layer — they live inside the database, not in your app code, so a bug in the app cannot bypass them.

| Entity | Member: read | Member: create | Member: update | Member: delete | Coach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| profiles | Own row only | ❌ Auto-created by DB trigger on sign-up | Own row — **role and Stripe fields are locked columns** | ❌ | All rows (full CRUD) |
| plan_templates | All rows, if subscription active | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | All rows (full CRUD) |
| exercises | All rows | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | All rows (full CRUD) |
| template_exercises | All rows, if subscription active | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | All rows (full CRUD) |
| workouts | Own rows only | Own rows | Own rows | ❌ | All rows |
| sets | Own rows only | Own rows | Own rows | Own rows | All rows |
| form_videos | **Own rows only — never another member's** | Own rows (status starts as `pending`) | ❌ Only the Edge Function's service key updates `ai_feedback` | ❌ | All rows (coach can review for feedback quality) |

> **"must NEVER" enforcement:** The `form_videos` RLS policy uses `WHERE member_id = auth.uid()`. No query from any member session — no matter what the app sends — can return a row belonging to another member. The only key that bypasses RLS is the service-role key, which lives only inside Edge Functions (section 4). The same `WHERE id = auth.uid()` pattern protects `profiles.weight_kg` and `profiles.measurements`.

---

## 4. Trust Boundaries

### The browser is untrusted

The PWA running in the phone's browser is untrusted. Anyone can open DevTools, inspect network requests, and read every value embedded in the JavaScript files. Nothing secret ever goes there.

**Safe to put in the browser:**
- Supabase **anon key** — designed to be public. It just tells Supabase which project you're connecting to. RLS rules, not this key, protect your data.
- The user's **session access token** (short-lived; see below)

**Must NEVER go in the browser:**
| Secret | Why it's dangerous if leaked |
|---|---|
| Supabase service-role key | Bypasses all RLS — gives read/write access to every row for every user |
| OpenAI API key | Anyone who has it can run API calls billed to you |
| Stripe secret key | Anyone who has it can issue refunds, read customer data, or cancel subscriptions |
| Stripe webhook secret | Lets an attacker forge payment confirmation events |

All four live only in Supabase Edge Function environment variables — a settings panel inside Supabase's dashboard that is never sent to any browser.

### Session token in the PWA (web-specific)

Supabase Auth stores the login session in **`localStorage`** — a browser storage area that JavaScript can read and write. This is less secure than an **httpOnly cookie** (a special browser cookie that JavaScript cannot read at all, making it much harder to steal), but httpOnly cookies require a server to set them, which adds significant complexity for a solo builder deploying a static Expo web app.

**How this risk is kept acceptable for V1:**
- Your app runs on HTTPS (enforced by Vercel) — the token cannot be intercepted in transit
- Supabase issues **access tokens that expire after 1 hour**, with a separate refresh token — even if a token is stolen, it stops working quickly
- Add these two headers to your `vercel.json` config (two lines of JSON) to block the most common attack vectors:
  - `X-Frame-Options: DENY` — prevents your app from being embedded in another site
  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` — prevents browsers from misinterpreting file types
- Supabase also supports a Content Security Policy header — a browser rule that blocks any script not explicitly on your approved list — reducing the risk of XSS (cross-site scripting: an attack where malicious code is injected into your page and reads `localStorage`)

### Where roles are stored

`profiles.role` lives in the PostgreSQL database. An RLS policy restricts `UPDATE` on `profiles` so that:

1. A member can update their own row (display name, weight, measurements)
2. The `role`, `stripe_customer_id`, `subscription_status`, and `subscription_id` columns are excluded from what members can update

The coach account is set directly in the Supabase dashboard (you flip `role` from `'member'` to `'coach'` manually, once). There is no sign-up flow that produces a coach. Members cannot escalate themselves.

### File storage — what's public vs. private

| Bucket | Contents | Public? | How accessed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `form-videos` | Uploaded form-check videos | ❌ Private | Signed URL — a temporary link generated by the Edge Function, valid for 1 hour maximum, only after verifying `member_id = auth.uid()` |
| `video-frames` | Still frames extracted from videos (used for AI) | ❌ Private | Same — signed URL, 1-hour expiry |
| `exercise-demos` | Coach's demo exercise clips | ✅ Public | Direct URL (no personal data) |

No personal file ever lives in a public bucket. A direct storage URL for a private bucket returns HTTP 403 Access Denied — there is no way to guess a path and view someone's video.

**Retention policy:** Set a 30-day automatic deletion lifecycle rule on `form-videos` and `video-frames` in Supabase Storage. The AI feedback text is kept in the database permanently; only the raw video and frame files are deleted.

### Payment confirmation

The subscription lock is set by the server, not by the browser. The exact flow:

1. Member clicks Subscribe → browser calls the `create-checkout` Edge Function
2. Edge Function creates a Stripe Checkout session (server-side) and returns a redirect URL
3. Member completes payment on **Stripe's hosted page** — outside your app
4. Stripe sends a **webhook** (an automatic notification Stripe pushes to your server when an event happens — like getting a text message saying "payment received" instead of you repeatedly calling Stripe to ask) to your `stripe-webhook` Edge Function, signed with the webhook secret
5. Edge Function verifies the signature and sets `profiles.subscription_status = 'active'`
6. App reads `subscription_status` from the database on every protected screen load

A member cannot unlock the app by changing anything in the browser. The unlock happens only after the database is updated by the Edge Function.

### Navigation and URLs

Since this is a PWA, "deep links" are regular HTTPS URLs (e.g., `https://formcoach.app/workout/today`). Every protected route calls `supabase.auth.getSession()` on load — if there is no valid session, the user is redirected to the login screen before any data is fetched. No URL skips this check.

## 7. Decisions Log

These are **final** unless you change them. An ADR (Architecture Decision Record) is a one-line note recording why a key choice was made — so you don't second-guess yourself six months from now.

1. **ADR-1:** Use PWA instead of a native app-store app because the goal of collecting Stripe subscriptions without a store cut is impossible inside a native app under current App Store and Google Play rules.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase for database, auth, storage, and edge functions because the user already has an account and it covers every backend need in one service within budget.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Supabase Row Level Security as the primary privacy-enforcement layer because it blocks unauthorised data access at the database level regardless of bugs in the application code.
4. **ADR-4:** Use Stripe Checkout (hosted payment page) because it offloads credit-card security compliance entirely to Stripe and works without modification in a web app.
5. **ADR-5:** Use OpenAI GPT-4o Vision with client-side frame extraction because it avoids complex video-processing libraries inside Edge Functions, which have CPU limits and a 60-second execution timeout.
6. **ADR-6:** Store all secret API keys exclusively in Supabase Edge Function environment variables because the browser is untrusted and any key shipped in the frontend can be extracted.
7. **ADR-7:** Use Vercel for frontend hosting because its free tier is sufficient for early growth and it deploys automatically from a Git push.
8. **ADR-8:** Store user videos in a private Supabase Storage bucket with a 30-day deletion policy, serve them only through 1-hour signed URLs, to enforce the "members must NEVER see other members' videos" rule.
9. **ADR-9:** Store `role` in `profiles.role` (database) with an RLS column-level restriction preventing members from updating it — not in browser storage or editable profile metadata.

- **All your data lives in Supabase, which acts like a locked filing cabinet with individual drawers for each member.** Each person can only open their own drawer. Your spec includes this note: *"I want to take the $9.99/month with Stripe inside the app so Apple and Google don't take a cut."* This creates a direct conflict with App Store rules that needs resolving before anything else.

**The problem:** Apple requires any app sold through the App Store that offers digital subscriptions to use Apple's own payment system (called In-App Purchases, or IAP). Apple takes 30% in year one and 15% after that for long-term subscribers. Google Play has the same rule with similar percentages. Putting a Stripe subscription button inside an App Store or Play Store app violates their guidelines and can get your app removed.
