### Access Rules

"RLS policy" = a rule written into the database so the database itself refuses the wrong request, even if the app code has a bug.

| Entity | Member: read | Member: create | Member: update | Member: delete | Coach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `profiles` | Own row only | Own row (via signup flow) | Own row — **`role` field is read-only to members** | No | Read all; set `role` |
| `measurements` | **Own rows only — never another member's** | Own rows | Own rows | Own rows | Read all |
| `plan_templates` | Read (to see their plan) | No | No | No | Full CRUD |
| `template_days` | Read | No | No | No | Full CRUD |
| `template_exercises` | Read | No | No | No | Full CRUD |
| `member_plans` | Own rows only | No | No | No | Full CRUD |
| `workouts` | Own rows only | No | Update `completed_at` only | No | Full CRUD |
| `sets` | Own rows only | Own rows | Own rows | Own rows | Read all |
| `form_videos` | **Own rows only — never another member's** | Own rows | No (Edge Function writes `ai_feedback` via service role) | Own rows | Read all |
| `subscriptions` | Own row only | No (Edge Function creates via webhook) | No (Edge Function updates only) | No | Read all |

---

## 4. Trust Boundaries

**"Untrusted"** = anything running on the user's device. Anyone can open browser developer tools, read all the code, and modify what the app sends to your server. Design accordingly.

**"Trusted"** = code running in Supabase Edge Functions on a server you control. Users cannot read or alter this code.

---

### Untrusted — User's Phone / Browser (the PWA)

Everything the Expo web build compiles and ships to the browser is untrusted:

- All React Native Web component code
- `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — these are **intentionally public**; the RLS policies do the real protection
- `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` — safe to expose; it can only initiate a payment session, not charge a card
- The user's JWT login token (see below)
- Any data the user types or records before it's sent

---

### Trusted — Supabase Edge Functions

Every sensitive action must live here and only here:

| What | Why it must be server-side |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Creates Checkout sessions, reads subscription data — exposing this lets anyone charge cards on your behalf |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Verifies that incoming webhook events genuinely came from Stripe and not an attacker |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | AI API key — exposed in the app would let anyone bill charges to your account |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Bypasses RLS — used only for operations that happen outside a user session (e.g., a Stripe webhook arrives with no logged-in user) |
| Stripe webhook verification | Forged webhooks could unlock subscriptions without payment |
| All AI calls | Never send an AI API key to the browser |
| Activating / revoking subscriptions | Must happen after server-side Stripe confirmation, never on the client's say-so |

---

### Where roles are stored and why users can't change their own

The `role` field is stored in **two places**, both server-controlled:

1. **Supabase Auth `app_metadata`** — a server-only field on the auth user object. Unlike `user_metadata` (which users *can* edit via the Supabase client), `app_metadata` can only be written using the service role key, which only lives in Edge Functions. The JWT token Supabase issues includes `app_metadata` claims, so Edge Functions and RLS policies read the role directly from the token without an extra database query.

2. **`profiles.role` in the database** — protected by an RLS policy that allows users to update their own row but explicitly blocks any change to the `role` column.

You set the coach role manually in the Supabase dashboard. All new sign-ups are `member` by default, set by a database trigger or Edge Function at sign-up time. There is no API endpoint, form field, or editable metadata that accepts a role value from the user.

---

### Where the login token lives in the browser (PWA)

When a user logs in, Supabase Auth returns a JWT (a signed digital pass, valid for 1 hour) and a longer-lived refresh token (used to silently get a new JWT when it expires). By default, the Supabase JS client stores both in `localStorage` — browser storage that JavaScript on your page can read.

This is standard practice for web apps and acceptable for a consumer fitness product. The main theoretical risk is a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack — if malicious JavaScript were injected into your page, it could read the token. The practical mitigation:

- Supabase's own libraries are well-audited
- Keep third-party JavaScript dependencies minimal
- Add a Content Security Policy (CSP) header — a browser rule that blocks scripts from unexpected sources — when you set up Vercel

The JWT expiring every hour limits damage from a stolen token. Because RLS ties every database row to `auth.uid()`, even a stolen member JWT only gives access to that member's own data.

---

### File storage — where files live and how they're accessed

| Location | Public? | How it's accessed |
|---|---|---|
| Supabase Storage — `videos` bucket | **Private** | Signed URLs only — a time-limited link (expires in 1 hour) generated by an Edge Function *after* it verifies `form_videos.member_id = auth.uid()` |
| App icons, static images | Public | Direct URL — no personal data in these files |

The `storage_path` field in `form_videos` is an internal path, not a URL. The browser cannot construct a download link from it. To watch a video, the app calls an Edge Function with the video's `id`; the function checks the database (via RLS) that the requester owns that video, then calls the Supabase Storage API to generate a signed URL, which it returns to the app. A different member's video ID returns a 403 (access denied), not a URL.

---

### Build-tool caveat

Claude Code / Expo can scaffold `.env` files and suggest putting API keys in `app.config.js` or `expo-constants`. **Never put `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, or `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in any file inside your Expo project, in source control, or in Vercel's public environment variable panel.** These three keys go into **Supabase Edge Function Secrets** only, set in the Supabase dashboard under Edge Functions → Secrets.

---

## 5. External Services

"Free tier" = what a service allows before it starts charging. "Webhook" = a notification a third-party service sends to your server when something happens.

| Service | Purpose | Key(s) | Where key lives | Free tier / pricing | If it goes down |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions — your entire backend | `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (public, safe in app) / `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (secret, Edge Functions only) | Public keys compiled into app; service role key in Edge Function Secrets only | Free: 500 MB DB, 5 GB storage, 5 GB bandwidth, 500K Edge Function calls. **Pro: $25/month** — needed before your first paying user uploads videos | Entire app is down. Monitor status.supabase.com; this is the single-dependency risk you accept (see §8) |
| **Stripe** | $9.99/month subscriptions, Checkout hosted payment page, subscription lifecycle webhooks | `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` (in app, safe) / `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (Edge Functions only) | Edge Function Secrets | No monthly fee; per-transaction card processing fees — check stripe.com/pricing for current rates, they change | New subscribers can't pay; existing active subscribers keep access until their `current_period_end` passes |
| **Google Gemini 1.5 Flash** | AI form video analysis — accepts raw video, returns feedback text | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Edge Function Secrets only — never in the app | Free tier: 15 requests/min, 1 million tokens/day. Paid: ~$0.075/1M input tokens; a 10-second video ≈ 2,600 tokens ≈ **$0.003 per form check**. Check ai.google.dev for current pricing | Show "analysis is queued" in the app; the Edge Function retries automatically; feedback is delayed, not lost |
| **Vercel** | Hosts and serves the PWA | No key in the app; auth handled via Vercel CLI login | n/a | Free tier covers most small apps (100 GB bandwidth, unlimited deployments, custom domain + HTTPS) | App files are unreachable; users see a blank screen. Set up Vercel status alerts |
| **Resend** | Transactional email — subscription receipts, workout reminders, onboarding | `RESEND_API_KEY` | Edge Function Secrets | Free: 3,000 emails/month, 1 sending domain | Non-critical emails queue or drop; Auth emails (handled by Supabase) still work separately |

---

### On Apple and Google payment rules

Because FormCoach is a PWA — a website users add to their home screen — **Apple's In-App Purchase rules and Google Play's billing requirements do not apply**. Those rules only govern apps distributed through their stores. Stripe is a standard internet payment processor, the same as any e-commerce website. You keep 100% of revenue minus Stripe's per-transaction processing fee.

If you later publish a native app to either store, revisit this section. These rules change frequently and you must check the current App Store Review Guidelines and Google Play Billing Policy before submitting.

---

## 6. Cost at 0 / 100 / 1,000 Users

"Infrastructure cost" = what you pay for servers and services, separate from Stripe processing fees (which come out of revenue, not your pocket separately).

| | 0 users — dev | 100 subscribers | 1,000 subscribers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supabase | $0 (free) | $25/month (Pro — needed once video storage accumulates and you want daily backups) | $25/month (Pro includes 100 GB storage, 250 GB bandwidth — sufficient) |
| Vercel | $0 | $0 (free tier — app bundle is static files, low bandwidth) | $0 |
| Google Gemini | $0 | ~$1/month (~2,000 form checks/month × $0.003) | ~$10/month (~20,000 checks) |
| Resend | $0 | $0 (free tier) | $0 (free tier) |
| Domain name | ~$12/year | same | same |
| **Total infrastructure** | **≈ $0** | **≈ $26/month** | **≈ $35/month** |
| Stripe fees (from revenue) | — | ~$60 taken from $999 revenue | ~$600 taken from $9,990 revenue |
| **Net monthly revenue** | — | **~$939** | **~$9,390** |

**Notes:**
- If members frequently rewatch old form videos, Supabase Storage bandwidth add-ons ($0.09/GB beyond the 250 GB included) could add $10–30/month at 1,000 users. Still comfortably within your $75 budget.
- A 90-day video retention policy (auto-delete raw video, keep AI feedback text forever) would cap storage costs permanently. Recommended.
- You stay under $75/month well past 1,000 paying users.

---

## 7. Decisions Log

These are final unless you explicitly change them in a later session.

- **ADR-1:** Build a PWA instead of an App Store / Play Store app, because the user requires Stripe subscriptions, which are incompatible with App Store and Play Store payment rules.
- **ADR-2:** Use Supabase as the single backend platform (database, auth, storage, edge functions), because the user already has an account and consolidating everything in one service minimises the number of accounts, bills, and failure points.
- **ADR-3:** Enforce member data isolation with Supabase RLS policies at the database level, because application-layer checks can be bypassed by bugs; database-level rules cannot.
- **ADR-4:** Store the user role in Supabase Auth `app_metadata` (server-set, user-cannot-edit) and mirror it in `profiles.role` with an RLS guard, because this is the only reliable way to prevent a member from elevating their own permissions.
- **ADR-5:** Use Google Gemini 1.5 Flash for form video analysis, because it accepts raw video natively, costs ~$0.003 per form check, and has a generous free tier.
- **ADR-6:** Use Stripe Checkout (Stripe's hosted payment page) for subscriptions, because card data never touches the server and reduces PCI compliance (the rules for handling card data) burden to near zero.
- **ADR-7:** Store all form videos in a private Supabase Storage bucket and serve only via signed URLs expiring in 1 hour, because members must never see another member's videos.
- **ADR-8:** Keep all secret keys (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) in Supabase Edge Function Secrets only — never in the Expo project, source control, or public Vercel env vars.
- **ADR-9:** Use Vercel for PWA hosting, because its free tier is sufficient through early growth and deployment is a single CLI command.

---

## 8. Known Risks

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Video recording in iPhone's browser** — Safari on iPhone applies stricter limits to `MediaRecorder` (the browser API for capturing video). Older iOS versions or Low Power Mode may silently fail or produce a file Gemini can't read. | Medium — iPhone is a primary target device | Test on a real iPhone in week one of building. Enforce a 10-second / 20 MB cap. Compress video client-side before uploading. Provide a fallback: if recording fails, let the member pick a video from their camera roll instead. |
| **2** | **AI feedback quality disappoints users** — Gemini may return generic, overly cautious, or outright wrong form advice on a 10-second clip. Poor feedback will churn paying members fast. | High at launch without investment in prompting | Spend serious time on the system prompt you send Gemini (e.g., describe the exercise, the camera angle, what good form looks like). Add a "Coach-reviewed" flag to the `form_videos` table. In the first month, review all AI feedback yourself before it appears to members. |
| **3** | **Supabase is a single point of failure** — your database, auth, storage, and API all run in one service. An outage takes down the entire app. | Low — Supabase's Pro plan SLA is strong | Monitor status.supabase.com and enable alerts. This is an acceptable trade-off for a solo builder at this stage. Do not attempt to multi-cloud until revenue justifies it. |
| **4** | **Stripe webhook missed or delayed** — Stripe sends a webhook to confirm payment. If your Edge Function is briefly unavailable, the subscription won't activate instantly. Stripe retries for up to 72 hours. | Low — Edge Functions are highly available | Store raw webhook events in a `webhook_log` table and process them idempotently (processing the same event twice should produce the same result with no double-activation). Supabase Edge Functions restart quickly and the retry window is long. |
| **5** | **Video storage grows without a ceiling** — at 5 MB per video and 5 uploads/week per member, 100 members generate ~10 GB/month. Costs stay low today but compound without a policy. | Medium — depends on member activity | Implement a 90-day retention policy at launch: auto-delete the raw video file from Storage after 90 days (the AI feedback text and metadata stay forever). Surface this clearly in the app's privacy notice. Add a per-member monthly video quota if needed. |

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **One service handles almost everything.** Supabase is your database, your login system, your video storage locker, and the place your business logic runs. You don't need to stitch together six accounts and keep them talking to eachother — one account, one dashboard, one bill.

- **No one can see another member's videos or body measurements, ever — and this is enforced at the deepest possible level.** The database itself is programmed to refuse any request for data that doesn't belong to the person asking. Even if there is a bug in the app code, the database says no.

- **Your card-taking happens entirely on Stripe's website.** When someone subscribes, they briefly leave your app, enter their card details on Stripe's page, and come back. You never see their card number and are not responsible for protecting it.

- **Stripe does not take a cut.** Because this is a website people add to their home screen — not an App Store or Play Store app — Apple's and Google's payment rules do not apply. The only fee is Stripe's standard card processing charge (roughly $0.59 on a $9.99 charge); the rest is yours.

- **You can fix bugs and ship features instantly.** Changes go live the moment you deploy to Vercel — no waiting for Apple or Google to review them. At 1,000 paying members your infrastructure costs roughly $35/month against nearly $9,400 in monthly revenue.

---

## 10. Accounts to Set Up Before Building

No Apple Developer Program or Google Play Console needed on the PWA path — saves $99/year and eliminates review delays.

- [ ] **Supabase** — supabase.com — Free to create; you already have an account. Upgrade to **Pro ($25/month)** before your first paying member uploads videos. No approval wait.
- [ ] **Stripe** — stripe.com — You already have an account. Enable **Stripe Checkout** and **Stripe Billing** in the dashboard. Activate live mode (usually minutes; occasionally 1–2 business days if Stripe asks for identity verification).
- [ ] **Google AI Studio** — aistudio.google.com — Free to create a project and get a Gemini API key. Enable billing on Google Cloud Console before you exceed the free tier. No approval wait.
- [ ] **Vercel** — vercel.com — Free to create. Connect your GitHub repository. No approval wait.
- [ ] **Resend** — resend.com — Free tier. Add and verify your sending domain (requires a DNS record change; takes about 10 minutes once you know where your domain's DNS is managed). No approval wait.
- [ ] **Domain name** — strongly recommended; users install your PWA from this URL, so a real domain matters. ~$10–15/year from Namecheap, Cloudflare Registrar, or similar. No approval wait.

**Total upfront cost before writing a line of code:** ~$10–15 (domain). Everything else is free until you have paying users.

---

## Context Carry

**Platforms:** iPhone and Android, delivered as a Progressive Web App (PWA) — not in any app store.

**Stack:** Expo (React Native Web / PWA) → Vercel; Supabase (PostgreSQL + RLS, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions); Stripe Checkout + Billing + Webhooks; Google Gemini 1.5 Flash; Resend for transactional email.

**Entities:** `profiles`, `measurements` (sensitive), `plan_templates`, `template_days`, `template_exercises`, `member_plans`, `workouts`, `sets`, `form_videos` (sensitive), `subscriptions`.

**Trust-boundary rules:** All secret keys in Edge Function Secrets only — never in the app or source control. Role stored in `app_metadata` (server-set, user-cannot-edit) and mirrored in `profiles.role` with RLS guard. Videos in private Storage bucket, served via signed URLs expiring in 1 hour. Members see only their own rows — enforced by RLS at the database level, not app code.

**ADRs:** ADR-1 PWA not app store. ADR-2 Supabase single backend. ADR-3 RLS for data isolation. ADR-4 role in `app_metadata`. ADR-5 Gemini Flash for video AI. ADR-6 Stripe Checkout hosted. ADR-7 private storage + signed URLs. ADR-8 secrets in Edge Function Secrets only. ADR-9 Vercel for hosting.

# PLAN.md — FormCoach Build Plan

---

## Definition of Done — applies to every slice without exception

1. Zero console errors or warnings when the slice's feature is used.
2. Works on a real phone or the phone simulator at the **smallest supported screen size**: iPhone SE (375 × 667 logical points) and a 360 × 640 dp Android phone.
3. Only the approved design tokens are used for colour: `#F4F1EA` background, `#151515` text, `#FF5A1F` primary action, `#FFFFFF` surface. No inline hex values or third-party theme colours anywhere except `/constants/tokens.ts`.
4. Only the two approved fonts: **Archivo Black** (display headings) and **IBM Plex Sans** (all body text, 16 pt / 24 pt line height). No system fonts.
5. No gradients. All corner radii are 6 pt or 0. No exceptions.
6. Every touchable element is at least 48 × 48 pt.
7. **No secret keys in the app bundle.** The only Supabase key that may ship in the compiled app is the **anon key** (the public key that is safe to expose because Row Level Security enforces access — explained below). The OpenAI API key and Supabase service role key live only on the server.

---

## Milestone 0 — Project Skeleton, Design Tokens, and On-Device Boot

*Goal: a working shell that shows the design system and runs on a real phone. No features yet.*

-- If the private schema doesn't exist yet:
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS private;

-- Members (one row per user; contains sensitive body data)

);

-- Body measurements — kept separate from members because they are especially sensitive
CREATE TABLE public.body_measurements (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  member_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  measured_at date NOT NULL,

  created_at  timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

-- Workouts (one per day per member)

  id             uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  member_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scheduled_for  date NOT NULL,
  name           text NOT NULL,
  created_at     timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

-- Sets (individual set entries within a workout)

  workout_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.workouts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

);

  member_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  workout_id    uuid REFERENCES public.workouts(id),

  ai_feedback   text,             -- filled in by the Edge Function after AI analysis
  feedback_at   timestamptz,
  created_at    timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

-- Subscriptions (tracks active $9.99/month status)
CREATE TABLE public.subscriptions (
  id                     uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  member_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  is_active              boolean DEFAULT false,

### [ ] M1-S2 — Row Level Security policies

**Goal:** Add database rules so every member can only read and write their own rows — no member can ever see another member's data.

*(RLS = Row Level Security: a Postgres feature that automatically filters query results based on who is logged in. It acts like an invisible WHERE clause on every query.)*

**Build prompt:**

```
In the Supabase SQL Editor, run the following. Save as /supabase/migrations/002_rls.sql.

-- Enable RLS on every public table.
-- Default-deny: once enabled, NO data is readable until a policy explicitly allows it.
ALTER TABLE public.members            ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.body_measurements  ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.workouts           ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.sets               ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.videos             ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.subscriptions      ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- members: each user sees and modifies only their own row
CREATE POLICY "member_own" ON public.members
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = id);

-- body_measurements: own rows only — these are sensitive
CREATE POLICY "bm_own" ON public.body_measurements
  FOR ALL```sql
  USING (auth.uid() = member_id);

-- workouts: own rows only
CREATE POLICY "workout_own" ON public.workouts
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = member_id);

-- sets: own rows only
CREATE POLICY "set_own" ON public.sets
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = member_id);

-- videos: own rows only — CRITICAL, members must NEVER see other members' videos
CREATE POLICY "video_own" ON public.videos
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = member_id);

-- subscriptions: own rows only
CREATE POLICY "sub_own" ON public.subscriptions
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = member_id);
```

### [ ] M1-S3 — Private video storage bucket and signed-URL helper

**Goal:** Create a storage bucket where videos are private and only accessible via short-lived signed URLs. *(A signed URL is a temporary link that expires after a set time, so videos cannot be accessed permanently.)*

**Build prompt:**

```

  Public:      OFF  ← private; no direct URL access

  MIME types:  video/mp4, video/quicktime

-- Members may upload only to their own folder: videos/{their_member_id}/
CREATE POLICY "video_upload_own" ON storage.objects
  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (
    bucket_id = 'videos'
    AND auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]
  );

-- Members may read only their own objects
CREATE POLICY "video_read_own" ON storage.objects
  FOR SELECT USING (
    bucket_id = 'videos'
    AND auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]
  );

-- Members may delete only their own objects (needed for account deletion)
CREATE POLICY "video_delete_own" ON storage.objects
  FOR DELETE USING (
    bucket_id = 'videos'
    AND auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]
  );

### [ ] M1-S6 — Log-out and navigation guard

**Goal:** Members can log out; the app never shows protected screens to unauthenticated users.

**Build prompt:**

Create /hooks/useSession.ts:

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { Session } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
import { supabase } from '../lib/supabase';

export function useSession(): Session | null {
  const [session, setSession] = useState<Session | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    supabase.auth.getSession().then(({ data }) => setSession(data.session));
    const { data: sub } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((_e, s) => setSession(s));
    return () => sub.subscription.unsubscribe();
  }, []);
  return session;
}

### [ ] M2-S5 — AI form feedback Edge Function

**Goal:** A server-side function receives the video ID, calls OpenAI, and saves three bullet points of feedback.

*(An Edge Function is a small program that runs on Supabase's servers, never on the phone. It is the only place where secret API keys are used.)*

**Build prompt:**

```
Create /supabase/functions/check-form/index.ts:

import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts';
import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2';

const OPENAI_KEY  = Deno.env.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')!;       // secret; never in the app
const SUPA_URL    = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!;
const SERVICE_KEY = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!;  // server-only

serve(async (req) => {
  // 1. Authenticate the caller
  const auth = req.headers.get('Authorization');
  if (!auth) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });

  const userClient = createClient(SUPA_URL, Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_ANON_KEY')!, {
    global: { headers: { Authorization: auth } },
  });
  const { data: { user }, error: authErr } = await userClient.auth.getUser();
  if (authErr || !user) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });

  // 2. Daily limit: max 5 form checks per member per calendar day (per ADR-4)
  const admin = createClient(SUPA_URL, SERVICE_KEY);
  const todayStart = new Date(); todayStart.setHours(0,0,0,0);
  const { count } = await admin
    .from('videos')
    .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
    .eq('member_id', user.id)
    .gte('created_at', todayStart.toISOString())
    .not('ai_feedback', 'is', null);
  if ((count ?? 0) >= 5)
    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: 'daily_limit_reached' }), { status: 429 });

  // 3. Get and verify ownership of the video
  const { video_id } = await req.json();
  const { data: video } = await admin
    .from('videos')
    .select('storage_path')
    .eq('id', video_id)
    .eq('member_id', user.id)    // CRITICAL ownership check
    .single();
  if (!video) return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });

  // 4. Generate a short-lived signed URL for OpenAI to fetch the video
  const { data: signed } = await admin.storage
    .from('videos')
    .createSignedUrl(video.storage_path, 300);   // 5-minute window

  // 5. Call OpenAI Vision (gpt-4o)
  const aiRes = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${OPENAI_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: 'gpt-4o',
      messages: [{
        role: 'user',
        content: [
          { type: 'text', text: 'You are a personal trainer reviewing a short exercise form video. Give exactly 3 bullet points of concise, actionable feedback. Be encouraging but specific. Start each bullet with •' },
          { type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: signed!.signedUrl } },
        ],
      }],
      max_tokens: 300,
    }),
  });
  const ai = await aiRes.json();
  const feedback = ai.choices?.[0]?.message?.content ?? 'Unable to analyse video.';

  // 6. Save feedback to the video row
  await admin.from('videos')
    .update({ ai_feedback: feedback, feedback_at: new Date().toISOString() })
    .eq('id', video_id);

  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ feedback }), {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
});

Deploy:
  supabase functions deploy check-form

Set server secrets (run in your terminal — these values never go in the app):
  supabase secrets set OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
  supabase secrets set SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<service role key from Supabase Settings → API>
```

**How to test (terminal curl commands):**
```bash
# 1. No auth header → must return 401
curl -X POST https://<project>.supabase.co/functions/v1/check-form \
  -d '{"video_id":"any"}'

# 2. Own video_id with valid JWT → must return feedback JSON
curl -X POST https://<project>.supabase.co/functions/v1/check-form \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your JWT>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"video_id":"<your video row ID>"}'

# 3. Another member's video_id → must return 404
```

**Done when:** Returns three `•` bullet points. Returns 401 with no auth. Returns 404 for another member's video. Returns 429 after 5 calls in one day. OpenAI key visible only in Supabase secrets dashboard, not in any app file.

    const now = new Date();
    const day = now.getDay();  // 0 = Sunday
    const monday = new Date(now);
    monday.setDate(now.getDate() - ((day + 6) % 7));   // roll back to Monday

### [ ] M3-S4 — RevenueCat webhook and server-side subscription verification

**Goal:** A Supabase Edge Function receives purchase events from RevenueCat and keeps the `subscriptions` table accurate. The check-form function then verifies subscription server-side.

*(A webhook is an automated HTTP call that RevenueCat makes to your server whenever a purchase, renewal, or cancellation event occurs.)*

**Build prompt:**

```
Create /supabase/functions/revenuecat-webhook/index.ts:

import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts';
import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2';

const WEBHOOK_SECRET = Deno.env.get('REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET')!;
const SUPA_URL       = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!;
const SERVICE_KEY    = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!;

serve(async (req) => {
  if (req.headers.get('Authorization') !== WEBHOOK_SECRET)
    return new Response('Forbidden', { status: 403 });

  const event = await req.json();
  const { type, app_user_id, expiration_at_ms } = event;

  const admin = createClient(SUPA_URL, SERVICE_KEY);
  const isActive  = ['INITIAL_PURCHASE','RENEWAL','PRODUCT_CHANGE','UNCANCELLATION'].includes(type);
  const isExpired = ['EXPIRATION','CANCELLATION','BILLING_ISSUE'].includes(type);

  if (isActive || isExpired) {
    await admin.from('subscriptions').upsert(
      {
        member_id:              app_user_id,
        revenuecat_customer_id: app_user_id,
        is_active:              isActive,
        expires_at:             expiration_at_ms ? new Date(expiration_at_ms).toISOString() : null,
        updated_at:             new Date().toISOString(),
      },
      { onConflict: 'member_id' }
    );
  }
  return new Response('OK', { status: 200 });
});

### [ ] M7-S1 — In-app account deletion

**Goal:** Members can permanently delete their account and all data from inside the app. Apple requires this for any app that allows account creation.

**Build prompt:**

```
Create /supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts:

import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts';
import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2';

serve(async (req) => {
  const auth = req.headers.get('Authorization');
  if (!auth) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });

  const SUPA_URL    = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!;
  const SERVICE_KEY = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!;

  const userClient = createClient(SUPA_URL, Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_ANON_KEY')!, {
    global: { headers: { Authorization: auth } },
  });
  const { data: { user }, error } = await userClient.auth.getUser();
  if (error || !user) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });

  const admin = createClient(SUPA_URL, SERVICE_KEY);

  // Delete all videos from storage (list then delete)
  const { data: files } = await admin.storage.from('videos').list(user.id);
  if (files && files.length > 0) {
    const paths = files.map(f => `${user.id}/${f.name}`);
    await admin.storage.from('videos').remove(paths);
  }

  // Delete the auth user — ON DELETE CASCADE handles all public table rows
  await admin.auth.admin.deleteUser(user.id);

  return new Response('Deleted', { status: 200 });
});

- **Build prompt:**
  ```

  -- Enable UUID generation
  create extension if not exists "uuid-ossp";

  -- 1. profiles  (one row per auth user; stores role and body stats)
  create table public.profiles (
    id            uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
    role          text not null default 'member' check (role in ('member','coach')),
    weight_kg     numeric,
    measurements  jsonb
  );
  alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
  create policy "profiles: own row only"
    on public.profiles for all
    using (auth.uid() = id)
    with check (auth.uid() = id);

  -- 2. plan_templates  (coach creates; members read)
  create table public.plan_templates (
    id          uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),
    name        text not null,
    created_by  uuid references public.profiles(id),
    body        jsonb not null   -- array of 7 day objects
  );
  alter table public.plan_templates enable row level security;
  create policy "templates: coach write"
    on public.plan_templates for all
    using  ((select role from public.profiles where id = auth.uid()) = 'coach')
    with check ((select role from public.profiles where id = auth.uid()) = 'coach');
  create policy "templates: member read"
    on public.plan_templates for select
    using (auth.uid() is not null);

  -- 3. member_plans  (links a member to a template)

  create policy "member_plans: own row"
    on public.member_plans for all
    using (auth.uid() = member_id)
    with check (auth.uid() = member_id);
  create policy "member_plans: coach all"
    on public.member_plans for all

  -- 4. workouts  (one per day per member)
  create table public.workouts (

    date        date not null,

  alter table public.workouts enable row level security;

  -- 5. sets  (logged reps/weight per exercise)
  create table public.sets (

### S-12 — AI form-check Edge Function

- [ ] **S-12 AI feedback via Edge Function**
- **Goal:** After upload, an Edge Function (a small script that runs on Supabase's servers — you don't manage a separate server) calls OpenAI Vision with the video and writes structured feedback back to the videos row.
- **Build prompt:**
  ```
  Create supabase/functions/form-check/index.ts  (Deno runtime — Supabase Edge Functions use Deno,
  a JavaScript runtime, instead of Node.js):

  import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.177.0/http/server.ts";
  import { createClient } from "https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2";

  const OPENAI_KEY       = Deno.env.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")!;
  const SUPABASE_URL     = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_URL")!;
  const SUPABASE_SERVICE = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")!;
  const DAILY_LIMIT      = 5;

  serve(async (req) => {
    // Step 1 — verify caller is a signed-in member
    const token = req.headers.get("Authorization")?.replace("Bearer ", "") ?? "";
    const admin = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE);
    const { data: { user }, error: authErr } = await admin.auth.getUser(token);
    if (!user || authErr) return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });

    // Step 2 — parse body
    const { video_id } = await req.json() as { video_id: string };

    // Step 3 — fetch video row and confirm it belongs to this member
    const { data: vid, error: vidErr } = await admin
      .from("videos").select("*").eq("id", video_id).eq("member_id", user.id).single();
    if (!vid || vidErr) return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });

    // Step 4 — enforce 5 checks/day limit (ADR-4)
    const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
    const { count } = await admin.from("videos")
      .select("id", { count: "exact", head: true })
      .eq("member_id", user.id)
      .not("feedback", "is", null)
      .gte("uploaded_at", today);
    if ((count ?? 0) >= DAILY_LIMIT)
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: "Daily limit reached" }), { status: 429 });

    // Step 5 — confirm active subscription
    const { data: sub } = await admin.from("subscriptions")
      .select("status").eq("member_id", user.id).single();
    if (sub?.status !== "active")
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: "Subscription required" }), { status: 402 });

    // Step 6 — generate a 60-second expiring URL so OpenAI can read the private file
    const { data: signed } = await admin.storage
      .from("videos").createSignedUrl(vid.storage_path, 60);

    // Step 7 — call OpenAI Vision
    const oaRes = await fetch("https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${OPENAI_KEY}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        model: "gpt-4o",
        messages: [{
          role: "user",
          content: [
            { type: "text", text: "You are a strength-training coach. Analyse this workout video. Return valid JSON only with these keys: score (integer 1–10), positives (array of up to 3 short strings), corrections (array of up to 3 short strings), summary (one sentence, max 25 words). No prose outside the JSON." },
            { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: signed!.signedUrl } }
          ]
        }],
        max_tokens: 300,
      }),
    });
    const oaJson = await oaRes.json();
    let feedback: unknown;
    try { feedback = JSON.parse(oaJson.choices[0].message.content); }
    catch { feedback = { error: "Could not parse AI response" }; }

    // Step 8 — write feedback back to the videos row
    await admin.from("videos").update({
      feedback,
      checks_used: (vid.checks_used ?? 0) + 1,
    }).eq("id", video_id);

    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ feedback }), { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } });
  });

  ---
  Deploy the function:
    supabase functions deploy form-check --no-verify-jwt

  In Supabase dashboard → Settings → Edge Functions → Environment Variables, add:
    OPENAI_API_KEY = <your OpenAI key>
  This key NEVER goes in the app.

  import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.177.0/http/server.ts";

      Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")!
    );

    const newStatus = ["INITIAL_PURCHASE","RENEWAL","REACTIVATED"].includes(type)
      ? "active" : "inactive";

    await admin.from("subscriptions").upsert({
      member_id:      uid,
      rc_customer_id: event.id,
      status:         newStatus,
      product_id:     event.product_id ?? "formcoach_monthly_999",
      updated_at:     new Date().toISOString(),
    }, { onConflict: "member_id" });

    return new Response("OK");
  });

    import NetInfo from '@react-native-community/netinfo';
    import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
    export function useNetworkStatus() {
      const [isConnected, setIsConnected] = useState(true);

      }, []);

    2. If the Supabase query returns a non-null error:

### S-24 — In-app account deletion

- [ ] **S-24 Account deletion (required by Apple guideline 5.1.1)**
- **Goal:** Any member can permanently delete their account and all their data from inside the app.
- **Build prompt:**
  ```
  Create supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts:

  import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.177.0/http/server.ts";
  import { createClient } from "https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2";

  serve(async (req) => {
    const token = req.headers.get("Authorization")?.replace("Bearer ", "") ?? "";
    const admin = createClient(
      Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_URL")!,
      Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")!
    );
    const { data: { user } } = await admin.auth.getUser(token);
    if (!user) return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });

    // Deleting the auth user cascades to profiles, which cascades to workouts,
    // sets, videos, subscriptions via ON DELETE CASCADE defined in S-07.
    const { error } = await admin.auth.admin.deleteUser(user.id);
    if (error) return new Response(error.message, { status: 500 });

    return new Response("Deleted", { status: 200 });
  });

  Deploy: supabase functions deploy delete-account --no-verify-jwt

  ---
  In AccountScreen.tsx, below the "Log out" button add:

    A text link "Delete my account"
      (IBMPlexSans_400Regular 14, colour #D93025, marginTop 24, minHeight 48).

        "Delete account?",
        "This permanently deletes your account, all workouts, videos, and measurements. This cannot be undone.",
        [
          { text: "Cancel", style: "cancel" },
          {
            text: "Delete permanently", style: "destructive",
            onPress: async () => {
              const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
              const res = await fetch(
                `${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/delete-account`,
                { method: "POST",
                  headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${session!.access_token}` } }
              );
              if (res.ok) {
                await supabase.auth.signOut();
                navigation.reset({ index: 0, routes: [{ name: 'SignIn' }] });
              } else {
                Alert.alert("Error", "Could not delete your account. Please try again.");
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      );

## 14-Item Security Checklist

**1. SECRETS — ISSUE** (`.env` line 2; `app.config.js` line 9): An OpenAI secret key is exposed via `EXPO_PUBLIC_` (which bakes it into the app binary) and a Supabase service-role key is hard-coded in `app.config.js extra`.

**2. DATABASE ACCESS — ISSUE** (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`): `care_logs` has no row-level security (RLS — the database rule that controls which rows each user may see). The `profiles` update policy has no column restriction, so any user can flip `is_premium` on their own row.

**3. AUTHORIZATION — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`; `admin-delete-user/index.ts`): The reset-password function checks nothing before resetting any account; the admin-delete function checks a role value that users can write themselves.

**4. INPUT — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`): The reset function validates neither the supplied user ID nor the new password server-side; no file-upload type or size checks are present anywhere in the server code.

**5. PAYMENTS — ISSUE** (`src/screens/Paywall.js`; `001_init.sql`): Purchase receipts are never verified with Apple or Google; the database policy also lets any user set `is_premium = true` on their own profile row directly.

**6. AI/LLM — ISSUE** (`.env`; `src/lib/ai.js`): The OpenAI key is in the app bundle; `diagnose()` is called straight from the client with no server-side rate limit, no server-side premium check, and no prompt isolation.

**7. RATE LIMITS & ABUSE — ISSUE** (`src/screens/Login.js`; `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`): No rate limits exist on login, sign-up, or the password-reset endpoint.

**8. HEADERS & CORS — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`; `admin-delete-user/index.ts`): Neither Edge Function (server code that runs in Supabase's cloud) sets security headers or validates request origin.

**9. DATA EXPOSURE — ISSUE** (`001_init.sql`; `supabase/storage.sql`): `care_logs` (including `home_address`) is readable by every logged-in user because RLS is missing; the plant-photo bucket is world-readable.

**10. DESTRUCTIVE OPS — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts` line 5): The admin-delete check reads `user_metadata`, a field any user can overwrite.

**11. FILE STORAGE — ISSUE** (`supabase/storage.sql` line 2): The `plant-photos` bucket is created with `public: true`, meaning every photo URL is permanently open to the entire internet.

**12. ROLES — ISSUE** (`src/screens/Admin.js` line 4; `admin-delete-user/index.ts` line 5): The admin role is stored in `user_metadata`, which users control. It must be in `app_metadata`, a field only the service-role API can write.

**13. SENSITIVE DATA — ISSUE** (`001_init.sql`; `storage.sql`; `app.config.js`): Unprotected home addresses in `care_logs`, home-interior photos in a public bucket, and an undeclared contacts permission all warrant a formal privacy/legal review.

**14. PHONE APP — ISSUE** (`.env`; `app.config.js`; `Login.js`; `Paywall.js`; `linking.js`): Two secret keys inside the binary; password saved to unencrypted AsyncStorage; purchases not server-verified; a deep link that routes directly to an unauthenticated password-reset endpoint; excessive background-location, contacts, and microphone permissions.

---

## Findings

| # | Issue | Severity | Where | Plain-English risk | Exact fix |
|---|-------|----------|-------|--------------------|-----------|
| 1 | Service-role key hard-coded in app bundle | **Critical** | `app.config.js` line 9; `src/lib/supabase.js` line 4 | The service-role key is a master key that turns off every database access rule. Anyone who downloads the app and unpacks the binary with a free tool reads this key, then reads, edits, or deletes every row in the database. | Use the public **anon key** (a limited key meant for clients) in the app. Remove `supabaseKey` from `extra`. Move any server-only operation to Supabase Edge Functions that read `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from Supabase's encrypted secret store — never from the app. Also add `.env` to `.gitignore`. |
| 2 | OpenAI API key bundled into the app | **Critical** | `.env` line 2; `src/lib/ai.js` line 5 | `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variables are copied verbatim into the compiled JavaScript bundle inside the `.ipa`/`.apk` file. Anyone who unpacks the file with a text editor reads the key and bills unlimited AI calls to your account. | Remove `EXPO_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY`. Create a `diagnose-plant` Edge Function that stores the key with `supabase secrets set OPENAI_KEY=...`. The app calls that function; the function calls OpenAI. The key never leaves the server. |
| 3 | Password-reset endpoint has no authentication at all | **Critical** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts` lines 4–5 | Anyone who knows or guesses a user's UUID can `POST { uid, newPassword }` to this endpoint and immediately own that account. No token, no session, nothing is checked. | Delete this function entirely. Use Supabase's built-in flow: call `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email)`, which emails the user a cryptographically signed link. When the user taps that link the app receives a valid session automatically; then call `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password: newPassword })`. Identity is proven by the signed link, not a bare ID. |
| 4 | `care_logs` table has no row-level security | **Critical** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no `enable row level security` line for `care_logs` | Any logged-in user can run `SELECT * FROM care_logs` and read every other user's notes and **home address**. | Add two lines to the migration: `alter table care_logs enable row level security;` followed by `create policy "own care logs" on care_logs for all using (auth.uid() = owner_id);` |
| 5 | Any user can set `is_premium = true` on their own row | **Critical** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` lines 10–11; `src/screens/Paywall.js` line 12 | The profile update policy covers every column with no restriction. Any logged-in user runs `supabase.from('profiles').update({ is_premium: true }).eq('id', myOwnId)` directly — no Paywall involved — and gets premium for free. | Replace the update policy so `is_premium` cannot be changed by the user: `create policy "own profile update" on profiles for update using (auth.uid() = id) with check (auth.uid() = id and is_premium is not distinct from (select is_premium from profiles where id = auth.uid()));` This lets users change `display_name` but freezes `is_premium` to its current server-set value. Only a server-side Edge Function (using the service-role key) should ever write that column. |
| 6 | Admin role stored in a field users can write themselves | **Critical** | `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts` line 5; `src/screens/Admin.js` line 4 | Supabase's `user_metadata` is writable by any authenticated user via `supabase.auth.updateUser({ data: { role: 'admin' } })`. After that one call the attacker passes the admin check on line 5 and can delete any account. | Move the role to `app_metadata` — a field only the service-role API can write, not users. Set it via the Supabase dashboard (Authentication → Users → edit a user). In `admin-delete-user/index.ts` line 5, change `user_metadata` to `app_metadata`: `if (user?.app_metadata?.role !== 'admin')`. |
| 7 | In-app purchase outcome never verified with Apple or Google | **Critical** | `src/screens/Paywall.js` lines 9–15 | The app trusts whatever the local store SDK returns. On a jailbroken or emulated device a mocked return makes the purchase look successful; `is_premium` is set to `true` and no money changes hands. | Create an Edge Function that: (1) receives the purchase receipt/token, (2) verifies it against Apple's `/verifyReceipt` endpoint or Google's `purchases.subscriptions.get` API, (3) only then calls `admin.from('profiles').update({ is_premium: true })` via the service role. The client must never write `is_premium` directly. |
| 8 | Password saved in plain, unencrypted local storage | **High** | `src/screens/Login.js` lines 12–13 | AsyncStorage stores data as plain text files on Android and does not use the secure Keychain on iOS. A device backup, a rooted device, or forensic software can read the saved password — one that the user likely reuses on other services. | Delete both `AsyncStorage.setItem('savedPassword', ...)` lines. You may keep `savedEmail` for form pre-fill. The Supabase client already stores the session token (a temporary proof of login) securely through its own storage adapter; there is no need to keep the password. |
| 9 | Plant-photo bucket is publicly accessible to anyone on the internet | **High** | `supabase/storage.sql` line 2 (`public: true`) | Every photo URL is permanently open worldwide with no login required. The file's own comment says these are photos "taken inside people's homes." | Change to `public: false`. Wherever the app needs to display a photo, generate a short-lived URL: `supabase.storage.from('plant-photos').createSignedUrl(path, 3600)` produces a link that expires after one hour. |
| 10 | Background location permission declared — not needed for a weather feature | **Medium** | `app.config.js` line 9 (`ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`) and line 8 (`NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`) | Background location tracks the device's GPS even when the app is closed. Checking the weather for a plant only needs location while the user has the app open. Declaring this permission also triggers a mandatory extended App Store review. | Remove `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` from Android and change the iOS key to `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`. Use `expo-location`'s `requestForegroundPermissionsAsync()`. |
| 11 | Contacts and microphone permissions declared with no matching feature in code | **Medium** | `app.config.js` lines 6, 7, 13, 14 | Requesting contacts reads the address book of every user — data about people who never consented. No contacts or voice-notes code appears anywhere in the files provided. Unused permissions increase legal exposure under GDPR and CCPA. | Remove `NSContactsUsageDescription`, `READ_CONTACTS`, `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, and `RECORD_AUDIO`. Add them back only when the feature is actually built, triggered at the moment the user first tries to use it, with a plain explanation. |
| 12 | No rate limiting on login or the password-reset endpoint | **Medium** | `src/screens/Login.js`; `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts` | Without limits an attacker can try thousands of passwords against a single account or hammer the reset endpoint in a loop. | Enable rate limiting in the Supabase dashboard under Authentication → Settings → Rate limits. After replacing the custom reset function with Supabase's built-in flow (fix #3), that flow is already rate-limited by email address. |

---

## Verdict: DO NOT SHIP

Seven Critical issues must be fixed before any users see this app. Two secret keys are extractable from the binary by anyone who downloads it. Any unauthenticated caller can take over any user's account by calling the password-reset endpoint with just a user ID. Every care log — including home addresses — is readable by every logged-in user. Any user can unlock premium or elevate themselves to admin with a single direct API call. And in-app purchases are never verified with the app stores. Fix these seven items first; the rest can follow in the same release cycle.

## Security Gate Review — PlantPal

**Architecture context:** ✓ Access rules and trust boundaries are present in the prompt.

Technical terms are explained in parentheses the first time they appear.

---

## 14-Point Checklist

**1. SECRETS — ISSUE** (`app.config.js`, `.env`, `src/lib/supabase.js`, `src/lib/ai.js`)
Two secret keys ship inside the app binary: the Supabase service-role key (a master key that bypasses every database access rule) is hardcoded in `app.config.js` and used as the client credential; the OpenAI key is in a variable prefixed `EXPO_PUBLIC_`, which Expo's bundler compiles into the JavaScript shipped on every device.

**2. DATABASE ACCESS — ISSUE** (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`)
`care_logs` never has Row Level Security (RLS — database rules that control which rows a user is allowed to see or change) switched on. The `profiles` update policy does not restrict which columns a user can change, leaving `is_premium` freely editable by any account owner.

**3. AUTHORIZATION — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`)
The password-reset Edge Function (a small server-side function hosted by Supabase) accepts a `uid` (the unique identifier Supabase assigns each user) and a new password from any caller without verifying that the caller owns that account.

**4. INPUT — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`, `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts`)
Neither Edge Function validates its inputs. No file-type or file-size restriction is visible for the storage bucket.

**5. PAYMENTS — ISSUE** (`src/screens/Paywall.js`)
After the device's purchase library returns any truthy result the app sets `is_premium = true` directly in the database without sending the receipt to Apple's or Google's servers for verification.

**6. AI/LLM — ISSUE** (`.env`, `src/lib/ai.js`)
The OpenAI key ships in the client bundle (see #1). `diagnose()` calls OpenAI directly from the device instead of through a server function, and contains no premium check or per-user rate limit before running.

**7. RATE LIMITS & ABUSE — ISSUE** (`src/screens/Login.js`, `supabase/functions/`)
No visible rate limiting on sign-in, sign-up, or either Edge Function. The AI endpoint is especially expensive per call.

**8. HEADERS & CORS — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/`)
Neither Edge Function sets explicit CORS (rules that control which callers can reach the server) or security headers. Supabase applies some defaults, but no policy is declared in code.

**9. DATA EXPOSURE — ISSUE** (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`, `supabase/storage.sql`)
`care_logs` rows including `home_address` are readable by any authenticated user because RLS is off. The plant-photos bucket is public, making every photo retrievable by anyone with a URL.

**10. DESTRUCTIVE OPS — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts`, `src/screens/Admin.js`)
`admin-delete-user` checks the admin role inside `user_metadata` (a user-editable field in Supabase), which any logged-in user can overwrite to gain admin power. The client-side `isAdmin()` check reads the same editable field.

**11. FILE STORAGE — ISSUE** (`supabase/storage.sql`)
`plant-photos` is created with `public: true`. Photos of home interiors are served to any unauthenticated HTTP request. No storage policies restrict who can upload or to which paths.

**12. ROLES — ISSUE** (`supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts`, `src/screens/Admin.js`)
Admin role is stored in `user_metadata`, which Supabase allows any authenticated user to overwrite via `supabase.auth.updateUser({ data: { role: 'admin' } })`. It must live in `app_metadata` (a server-only field only the service role can write).

**13. SENSITIVE DATA — ISSUE** (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`, `supabase/storage.sql`)
`home_address` is stored in `care_logs` with no access control. Home-interior photos are in a public bucket. Both are high-sensitivity personal data with no evidence of a GDPR/CCPA privacy review.

**14. PHONE APP — ISSUE** (`app.config.js`, `src/lib/supabase.js`, `src/screens/Login.js`, `src/screens/Paywall.js`, `src/linking.js`, `src/screens/Settings.js`)
Service-role key and OpenAI key are in the app bundle; the user's plaintext password is saved to AsyncStorage (unencrypted device storage); session tokens use AsyncStorage instead of the iOS Keychain / Android Keystore (the OS-level encrypted vaults built into each platform); purchases are not server-verified; the `reset-password` deep link passes a raw `uid` to an unauthenticated server function; `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` and `READ_CONTACTS` are declared but appear unnecessary; no in-app account-deletion flow exists (required by Apple and Google store policy).

---

## Findings Table

| # | Issue | Severity | Where | Plain-English risk | Exact fix |
|---|-------|----------|-------|--------------------|-----------|
| 1 | Supabase service-role key hardcoded in app bundle | **Critical** | `app.config.js` → `extra.supabaseKey`; consumed in `src/lib/supabase.js` | The service-role key skips every RLS rule. Anyone who unpacks the app binary (a five-minute job with freely available tools) gets permanent unrestricted read/write on all user data, can set any account to premium, and can read every home address and photo. | Remove `supabaseKey` from `extra`. Generate the `anon` key (the safe public key that respects RLS) from the Supabase dashboard and use that on the client. Any operation that genuinely needs the service role must live inside an Edge Function where the key is a private server-side environment variable (`Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')`). |
| 2 | OpenAI API key exposed in app bundle | **Critical** | `.env` → `EXPO_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY`; `src/lib/ai.js` line `Bearer ${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY}` | `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variables are compiled into the JavaScript shipped on every device. Anyone who opens the bundle with a text editor has the key and can run unlimited AI requests at the developer's expense with no cap. | Delete the variable from `.env`. Create a Supabase Edge Function that calls OpenAI using `Deno.env.get('OPENAI_KEY')`, verifies the caller's session JWT (the signed ticket proving who the user is), confirms `is_premium` server-side, then returns the result. The app calls the Edge Function — never OpenAI directly. |
| 3 | Password-reset Edge Function has no authentication | **Critical** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts` — the function reads no auth token; it accepts any `uid` and password from the request body | Any attacker who knows or guesses a user's UUID can POST `{ uid: "<victim>", newPassword: "hacked" }` and immediately take over that account. The deep link `plantpal://reset-password?uid=<userId>` makes this deliverable as a one-click link sent to the victim in a message. | Delete this function and the matching `ResetPassword` screen. Use Supabase's built-in flow: call `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email)`, let Supabase send a secure one-time link, then handle the session the link creates and call `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password: newPassword })`. No raw UID or password ever travels in a URL or request body. |
| 4 | Admin role stored in user-editable `user_metadata` | **Critical** | `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts` line `user?.user_metadata?.role !== 'admin'`; `src/screens/Admin.js` line `user?.user_metadata?.role === 'admin'` | Any logged-in user can call `supabase.auth.updateUser({ data: { role: 'admin' } })`, refresh their session to get a fresh JWT carrying the updated field, and then call `admin-delete-user` to delete any other user's account. This also unlocks the Admin screen via the `plantpal://admin` deep link. | Store the role in `app_metadata` instead — e.g., `app_metadata.role = 'admin'`. Supabase only allows the service role to write `app_metadata`, so users cannot change it themselves. Set admin status via a one-time server script or a protected admin console. Update both the Edge Function check and any server-side guard to read `user?.app_metadata?.role`. |
| 5 | User's plaintext password saved to AsyncStorage | **Critical** | `src/screens/Login.js` lines `AsyncStorage.setItem('savedPassword', password)` | AsyncStorage is an unencrypted SQLite file on Android. Anyone with a USB cable and Android Debug Bridge (ADB — a standard developer tool) on a backup-enabled or developer device can read the password without unlocking the phone. | Delete both `AsyncStorage.setItem('savedPassword', …)` lines. If you want to pre-fill the login form, save only the email address. Never store a password on the device under any circumstances. |
| 6 | `care_logs` table has no Row Level Security | **Critical** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no `ALTER TABLE care_logs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` statement | Every authenticated user can run `SELECT * FROM care_logs` and read all other users' notes and home addresses. The service-role key on the client (issue #1) makes this accessible even without authentication. | Add to a new migration file: `ALTER TABLE care_logs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` followed by `CREATE POLICY "own care_logs" ON care_logs FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = owner_id);` |
| 7 | `profiles` update policy lets any user set `is_premium = true` | **Critical** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — policy `"own profile update"` is unrestricted `FOR UPDATE` with no column filter | A user calls `supabase.from('profiles').update({ is_premium: true }).eq('id', myId)` and grants themselves premium without paying — no purchase required at all. | Replace the blanket update policy. The cleanest approach: remove `is_premium` from the user-writable surface entirely. Add a `WITH CHECK` clause so the column cannot change through a user's request: `CREATE POLICY "own profile update" ON profiles FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = id) WITH CHECK (is_premium = (SELECT is_premium FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid()));`. Only an Edge Function running with the service role may flip `is_premium`. |
| 8 | In-app purchase not verified server-side | **Critical** | `src/screens/Paywall.js` lines `if (purchase) { await supabase.from('profiles').update({ is_premium: true }) }` | Any truthy return from `requestSubscription()` — including a value from a patched app or a network proxy — immediately marks the account as premium. There is no check with Apple or Google that the transaction is real, paid, and linked to this user's account. | Create an Edge Function that receives the raw `transactionReceipt` (iOS) or `purchaseToken` (Android), calls Apple's `verifyReceipt` endpoint or the Google Play Developer API using a server-held secret, and only then sets `is_premium = true` using the service role. The client sends the receipt; the server makes the decision. Remove the client-side direct write to `is_premium` (pair with fix for issue #7). |
| 9 | Plant-photos storage bucket is public | **High** | `supabase/storage.sql` line `public: true` | Photos of the interiors of users' homes are served to any anonymous HTTP request. Anyone who finds or guesses a file path can download them. Without storage policies there is also no constraint on who may upload to whose folder. | Change the bucket declaration to `public: false`. Add storage policies restricting upload to the authenticated owner's folder (e.g., `WITH CHECK (auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1])`), and a matching read policy. Serve photos to the app via short-lived signed URLs (time-limited links that expire) generated by an Edge Function, never as permanent public URLs. |
| 10 | Session tokens stored in AsyncStorage instead of Keychain / Keystore | **Medium** | `src/lib/supabase.js` line `storage: AsyncStorage` | On a rooted Android device or a development iOS build, another process or a forensic tool can read the session token from unencrypted storage and impersonate the user until the token expires. | Replace `AsyncStorage` with `expo-secure-store`, which maps to the iOS Keychain and Android Keystore (the operating system's encrypted credential vaults). Pass a small custom storage adapter — wrapping `SecureStore.getItemAsync` / `setItemAsync` / `deleteItemAsync` — as the `storage` option to `createClient`. The Supabase React Native docs include a ready-made snippet. |
| 11 | `diagnose()` has no premium gate or per-user rate limit | **Medium** | `src/lib/ai.js` — no guard before the `fetch` call | Once AI calls are moved server-side (fix for issue #2), the Edge Function must still confirm the caller is premium and cap how many calls they can make per day. Without this, any logged-in user can use the paid feature for free and exhaust the AI budget. | Inside the AI Edge Function: (a) read `is_premium` from the database using the service role — never trust a value the client sends; (b) check a `daily_ai_calls` counter (a number in a database column that resets each day) and reject calls that exceed the limit before contacting OpenAI. |
| 12 | Excessive device permissions declared | **Medium** | `app.config.js` — `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`, `READ_CONTACTS` (Android); `NSContactsUsageDescription` (iOS) | Continuous background location and full contacts access are among the most privacy-sensitive permissions on both platforms. They increase App Store / Play Store scrutiny, require justification to regulators, and expand the blast radius if a third-party library in the project is ever compromised. | Remove `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` — weather needs only `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` while the app is in the foreground, not continuous background tracking. Remove `READ_CONTACTS` and `NSContactsUsageDescription` unless "Find friends" is a shipping feature; if it is, use the OS-provided contact picker (requires no permission for single selections on iOS 14+ and Android 13+). |
| 13 | No in-app account deletion | **Medium** | `src/screens/Settings.js` — comment "Delete account: users email support and we do it by hand" | Apple App Store guideline 5.1.1(v) and Google Play policy (enforced since June 2023) both require that any app offering account creation must provide in-app account deletion. Submitting without it results in rejection; existing apps can be removed from the stores. | Add a "Delete my account" option in Settings. On confirmation, it should call an authenticated Edge Function that verifies the user's JWT, deletes their data rows, removes their storage objects, and calls `admin.auth.admin.deleteUser(uid)` using the service role. |
| 14 | No rate limiting on login or expensive endpoints | **Medium** | `src/screens/Login.js` (login); future AI Edge Function | Without a limit on attempts, an attacker can try thousands of passwords against an account (brute force). The AI endpoint costs real money per call with no per-user cap. | Confirm that Supabase's built-in auth rate limiting is active in project settings (it is on by default but can be disabled). For the AI Edge Function, add a per-user daily call counter in the database (or use Supabase's function-level rate limiting) and return HTTP 429 when the limit is exceeded. |
| 15 | No explicit CORS policy on Edge Functions | **Low** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`, `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts` | Without a declared CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing — browser rules controlling which web pages may call your server) policy, any website could attempt to call these functions from a browser. This is low severity for a native mobile app, but matters if a web client is ever added. | Add a CORS preflight handler to each function and restrict `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to your own domain. Supabase's Edge Function documentation includes a standard CORS helper. |

---

## Ship Verdict: ⛔ DO NOT SHIP

There are **eight Critical issues**. Before any further testing, an attacker with the app installed can:

- Extract the service-role key from the binary and read or modify every user's record in the database
- Read every user's home address (no RLS on `care_logs`)
- Take over any account by calling the unauthenticated password-reset function directly or via a crafted deep link
- Escalate their own account to admin by writing `role: 'admin'` to their own `user_metadata`
- Grant themselves premium for free by writing `is_premium: true` directly, or by presenting a fake purchase receipt

## 14-Item Security Check

**Terminology note (first uses only):** *Service-role key* = the master Supabase key that bypasses every database access rule. *RLS (Row-Level Security)* = the database rule that says "you can only see your own rows." *AsyncStorage* = React Native's simple unencrypted key-value store. *APK/IPA* = the installable app package for Android / iPhone. *JWT* = a signed string used to prove who you are. *Edge Function* = serverless cloud code (Supabase's version). *Deep link* = a URL like `plantpal://something` that opens the app to a specific screen. *Receipt validation* = confirming with Apple's or Google's servers that a purchase actually happened.

---

1. **SECRETS — ISSUE** `.env`, `app.config.js`, `src/lib/ai.js` — OpenAI key exposed via `EXPO_PUBLIC_` prefix; Supabase service-role key hardcoded in `app.config.js extra`.
2. **DATABASE ACCESS — ISSUE** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `care_logs` is missing `enable row level security`; also moot while the service-role key is in the app (RLS is bypassed globally).
3. **AUTHORIZATION — ISSUE** `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts` — accepts any UID from the request body with no token or authentication check; also `src/screens/Admin.js` relies on a user-editable field.
4. **INPUT — ISSUE (Med)** No server-side validation visible anywhere; no storage upload policies defined in `supabase/storage.sql`, so any file type and size is accepted.
5. **PAYMENTS — ISSUE** `src/screens/Paywall.js` — `is_premium` is written directly from the client with no server-side receipt verification.
6. **AI/LLM — ISSUE** `.env`, `src/lib/ai.js` — OpenAI key is in the app bundle; AI calls are made from the client, not the server; no per-user rate limit.
7. **RATE LIMITS & ABUSE — ISSUE** No visible rate limiting on any custom endpoint; `reset-password` function is completely open.
8. **HEADERS & CORS — ISSUE (Low)** `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`, `admin-delete-user/index.ts` — no CORS preflight handler or security headers set in either Edge Function.
9. **DATA EXPOSURE — ISSUE** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `care_logs.home_address` is readable by any authenticated user because RLS is missing on that table (and bypassed globally via the service-role key).
10. **DESTRUCTIVE OPS — ISSUE** `src/screens/Admin.js`, `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts` — admin role check depends on `user_metadata` which users can write themselves.
11. **FILE STORAGE — ISSUE** `supabase/storage.sql` line 2 — `plant-photos` bucket is `public: true`; no upload policies defined; photos of people's home interiors are publicly accessible with no login.
12. **ROLES — ISSUE** `src/screens/Admin.js` `isAdmin()`, `admin-delete-user/index.ts` line 5 — role stored in `user_metadata`, which any user can update via `supabase.auth.updateUser()`.
13. **SENSITIVE DATA — ISSUE** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` (`home_address`), `app.config.js` (`READ_CONTACTS`) — full home addresses stored without minimization; contacts access declared; no privacy/legal review noted.
14. **PHONE APP — ISSUE** `app.config.js`, `src/lib/supabase.js`, `src/screens/Login.js`, `src/screens/Paywall.js`, `src/linking.js` — secret keys in the bundle; plaintext password in AsyncStorage; in-app purchase not server-verified; Admin screen reachable via deep link; background location and contacts permissions declared unnecessarily; no in-app account-deletion option.
