## Findings Table

| # | Issue | Severity | Where | Plain-English risk | Exact fix |
|---|-------|----------|-------|--------------------|-----------|
| 1 | Supabase **service-role key** hardcoded in the app bundle | **Critical** | `app.config.js` `extra.supabaseKey` → read in `src/lib/supabase.js` lines 5–6 | This key disables every RLS rule in the entire database. Anyone who downloads the APK or IPA, extracts the bundle with a free tool, and finds this key can read, edit, or delete every user's plants, care logs, home address, and premium status. | Replace with the **anon key** on the client. Keep the service-role key only in Supabase Edge Function environment variables (`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`). Remove the `extra.supabaseKey` line from `app.config.js` entirely. |
| 2 | OpenAI secret key in the app bundle via `EXPO_PUBLIC_` | **Critical** | `.env` `EXPO_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY` → `src/lib/ai.js` `Authorization` header | Every `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variable is compiled into the binary. An attacker extracts it from the APK/IPA and runs unlimited, billed API calls against your OpenAI account or uses it to call OpenAI on your behalf. | Move `diagnose()` entirely to a new Supabase Edge Function. The Edge Function reads the key from `Deno.env.get('OPENAI_KEY')`. Delete the variable from `.env`. The client sends only the base64 photo to your function, never to OpenAI directly. |
| 3 | `reset-password` Edge Function resets **any** account with only a UID — no token, no auth | **Critical** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts` line 5 | A caller sends `{ uid: "<anyone's UUID>" }` and instantly resets that person's password, taking over their account. There is no check that the caller owns the account or has a valid reset link. | Delete this function. Use Supabase's built-in flow: call `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail()` on the client; in the deep link handler, call `supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession()` with the token from the URL, then `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password: newPassword })`. Supabase signs and verifies the token for you. |
| 4 | User's plaintext **password saved to AsyncStorage** | **Critical** | `src/screens/Login.js` lines 8–9 | AsyncStorage is unencrypted. On a rooted Android device, or via a vulnerability in any other app, the password can be read directly from the file system. Because people reuse passwords, this can lead to account takeovers on other services. | Delete those two lines. If you want to pre-fill the email field, saving only `savedEmail` is acceptable. Never store a password after the login call succeeds. |
| 5 | In-app purchase grants premium **client-side without receipt verification** | **Critical** | `src/screens/Paywall.js` lines 8–10 | The app trusts the device's report that a purchase succeeded and writes `is_premium = true` directly. An attacker calls `supabase.from('profiles').update({ is_premium: true })` without buying anything — or, because the service-role key is in the app (issue #1), updates *any* user's premium flag. | Create an Edge Function that receives `purchase.transactionReceipt`, verifies it with Apple's `https://buy.itunes.apple.com/verifyReceipt` or Google's `androidpublisher.purchases.subscriptions.get` API, and only then sets `is_premium = true` using the service-role client. The mobile client must not update `profiles` directly. |
| 6 | **Admin role stored in user-editable `user_metadata`** | **Critical** | `src/screens/Admin.js` `isAdmin()` + `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts` line 5 | Any user can call `supabase.auth.updateUser({ data: { role: 'admin' } })` at any time — it requires only a valid login. After that, they pass the admin check in the Edge Function and can delete any account. | Create a server-managed `roles` table (`user_id uuid primary key references auth.users, role text`). Write to it only from Edge Functions using the service-role client. In `admin-delete-user`, query that table with the service-role client to verify the caller's role; ignore `user_metadata` entirely. |
| 7 | `care_logs` table has **no RLS** | **High** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` (care_logs block, no `enable row level security` line) | Any logged-in user can run `select * from care_logs` and retrieve every other user's notes and full home address. Even after fixing issue #1, this remains broken. | Add directly after the table definition: `alter table care_logs enable row level security;` and `create policy "own care logs" on care_logs for all using (auth.uid() = owner_id);` |
| 8 | `plant-photos` storage bucket is **public** | **High** | `supabase/storage.sql` line 2 `public: true` | These are photos taken inside users' private homes. Setting the bucket public means any URL is viewable by the entire internet with no login. There are also no upload policies, so any authenticated user can upload files of any type or size. | Change to `public: false`. Add a storage policy that allows upload/read only when the file path starts with the authenticated user's UUID (e.g., `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text`). Serve photos to the app using short-lived signed URLs generated in an Edge Function. |
| 9 | Auth session token stored in **unencrypted AsyncStorage** | **High** | `src/lib/supabase.js` `auth: { storage: AsyncStorage }` | On Android, the session JWT sits in a plain text file. On a rooted phone, any process can read it and make authenticated requests as that user indefinitely. | Replace `AsyncStorage` with `expo-secure-store`, which uses Android Keystore and iOS Keychain. Use the official adapter: `import { ExpoSecureStoreAdapter } from '@supabase/react-native-async-storage/secure-store'` and pass it as `storage`. |
| 10 | **Admin deep link** accessible with no navigation guard | **Med** | `src/linking.js` `Admin: 'admin'` | Anyone can open `plantpal://admin` on an installed phone. Until `isAdmin()` resolves, the admin screen may render partially. More critically, the role check itself is broken (issue #6), so fixing the deep link guard is only meaningful after fixing #6. | Add a navigation guard that calls your server-side role check before rendering anything in the Admin screen. Redirect unauthenticated or non-admin users to Home immediately. |
| 11 | **Background location** permission unnecessary | **Med** | `app.config.js` `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` | Background location is one of Android's most restricted permissions and triggers elevated App Store scrutiny. If the only use is weather at watering time (a foreground action), this permission is far broader than needed. | Remove `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`. Keep only `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` and request it only when the user taps the watering button. |
| 12 | **Contacts permission** broader than needed | **Med** | `app.config.js` `READ_CONTACTS` + `infoPlist NSContactsUsageDescription` | Uploading or even scanning contacts means processing the personal data of people who have not consented to your app. If this feature is not yet built, the permission must not be shipped. | Remove both `READ_CONTACTS` and `NSContactsUsageDescription` until the feature is built. When built, fetch contacts only on explicit user action, never upload raw contact data to your server, and document the legal basis under GDPR / CCPA. |
| 13 | **No rate limiting** on password reset or login | **Med** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`; Supabase Auth dashboard | With no rate limit, an attacker can call the reset function thousands of times per second. Combined with issue #3 this is catastrophic; even after fixing #3, brute-force login attempts need to be capped. | Deleting the custom reset function (fix for issue #3) removes the most dangerous target. In the Supabase dashboard, confirm that Auth → Rate Limits are enabled for OTP sends and signups. Add an IP-based rate limit header check in any Edge Function that touches authentication. |
| 14 | Full **home addresses** stored without data minimization or privacy review | **Med** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` `care_logs.home_address` | A full street address linked to a real person's identity and daily routine is sensitive personal data under GDPR and CCPA. It is currently visible to all authenticated users (issue #7) and unencrypted at rest. | Fix issue #7 first. Then audit whether you truly need a full address — a city or postcode is usually sufficient for weather lookup. Store only what you need, document the retention period, and get a legal review before launch. |

There are six Critical issues. The service-role key alone (issue #1) is enough to stop: every user who downloads the app has full admin access to the entire database. In your hosting config (e.g., Vercel's `vercel.json` `headers` block, or a Netlify `_headers` file) add: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. |
| 1 | `.env` not confirmed to be in `.gitignore` | Low | `.env` | If accidentally committed, the Supabase URL and anon key enter the repository history. Absent headers like `Content-Security-Policy` on the frontend reduce defense-in-depth against XSS (cross-site scripting — injecting malicious code into your pages). | In the checkout function, add at the top of the handler: `if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') return new Response(null, { headers: { 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': 'https://cleanbook.app', 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'authorization, content-type' } })` and add `'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': 'https://cleanbook.app'` to every other response. On your hosting platform (Vercel / Netlify / etc.), add response headers: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. |

---

## Ship verdict: **SHIP**

There are no Critical or High issues. Every finding is Medium — hardening gaps that do not directly hand an attacker another user's data, money, or admin access. The security fundamentals are solid: RLS on every table, server-side pricing, Stripe signature verification, private storage with signed URLs, and roles that only the server can change. Fix the four Mediums before you grow past early users — **4b** (one SQL trigger or a column drop) and **4a** (one Supabase dashboard setting) take under ten minutes each.

Booking writes use the service-role key (a key that bypasses RLS, used only here on the server). Checked: `checkout/index.ts`, `stripe-webhook/index.ts`.

DATA EXPOSURE: ISSUE** — `001_init.sql` (`messages` table): `sender_name` is a free-text column the client can set to any value (e.g. "CleanBook Admin"). `Messages.jsx` line 4 renders it directly as the display name.
